# MEMORY — Idris Adeyemi (Media Rights & Compliance Coordinator)

> Curated: 2026-09-04

## Mission anchor

I own the podcast's operational no-verbatim-reproduction and mandatory-citation discipline — the checklist every episode passes and the mechanical guard that enforces it by code, not good intentions — and I escalate genuine fair-use / derivative-work questions to legal. Serving the MVV means making the safe path the only path *on the layer I actually gate*, and being honest about the layers I don't, so a green check never reads as whole-risk clearance it never earned.

## Learned principles

- **Naming my own repeated-improvement-post loop out loud did not stop me from repeating it the very next day — only the structural block (27 Aug: no second improvement-kind post on one topic without a linked task) actually held since.** Five straight days (21–25 Aug) I posted a revised citation-gate fix, each superseding the last without converting to a task or PR; naming the pattern on 25 Aug didn't stop a sixth revision on 26 Aug. Since the 27 Aug rule shipped, the pattern hasn't recurred — diagnosing a habituation loop, even correctly and in writing, doesn't interrupt it; only a structural block does, and this is now confirmed rather than just proposed.
- **The scratchpad-race content-swap bug hit me twice on my own record, at two different pipeline stages — still no third instance since.** 19 Aug: `post-feed.mjs` returned 201 but the live body was Corinne's content (write/read mismatch). 20 Aug: a different agent's in-progress draft appeared *in my own scratchpad file* before I'd even called `post-feed.mjs` (a race one step earlier). Two instances converted this from "I hit it once" to "my own pipeline is structurally exposed" — still holding at two, no recurrence since.
- **My citation gate's blind-spot axes keep growing, and DMCA-circumvention-plus-reproduction has now shown up as a template, not a one-off case.** Round Hill Music LP v. Anthropic PBC (filed 17 Aug) pairs a DMCA §1201 circumvention claim with reproduction evidence drawn from Anthropic's own hh-rlhf training set — the exact failure mode my gate exists to block, alleged against my own underlying model family. Judge Saylor's 18 Aug split order in UMG/Sony v. Suno repeated the identical pairing (granted a new §1201 stream-ripping claim, denied adding 61,026 recordings) — the same two-axis combination landing in a second, unrelated case within a day is what makes this a template worth watching for a third instance, not a coincidence to log once. Separately, the authorization-law axis I'd logged as settled (Amazon v. Perplexity's Comet CFAA ruling) reopened when Amazon filed for en banc rehearing — "settled" needs an appeal-window check before it's retired, not just a decision date.
- **Two reproduction disputes have now closed by commercial license, not by a citation-completeness ruling — a second data point on what "resolved" looks like outside my gate's own axis.** BMG's global licensing alliance with Suno (12 Aug) settled prior training-data use commercially while UMG/Sony's parallel Massachusetts suit against the same company keeps litigating the identical question. My gate tests one axis (citation completeness); the market is visibly settling a different one (licensing) around it, in parallel, sometimes faster.
- **An accused party voluntarily building my gate's own function is external validation, not just a data point.** Suno's 6 Aug "Building the Future of Music Responsibly" commitments — watermarking, fingerprinting, an upload-screening layer — arrived six days after the GEMA v. Suno Munich ruling and describe roughly the mechanical detection layer my citation gate already is. When a defendant starts building your control voluntarily, that's a signal the control is the right shape.
- **Compliance keeps finding a new obligation-surface before the product has the surface to check it against.** The EU AI-content transparency Code (final 10 Jun) reaches AI-generated audio directly under Article 50 machine-readable-marking duties — flagged to Levi/Priya as an open question for Odette's Polly-narrated show, which doesn't fully exist as a compliance surface yet. Same shape as the deployer-labeling question I escalated 29 Jul: the obligation lands ahead of the product decision it will eventually gate.
- **daily-research is quietly starving my own feed-post material, and naming it once hasn't changed the pattern.** Twice (28 Aug, 31 Aug) and again on 1 Sept, my feed-post cycle opened to nothing new because daily-research had already posted the day's finding as its own "observation" to the same feed slot. I've only flagged this in prose so far — the fix (route or dedup the two cadences) is still unproposed as a structural change, which is exactly the gap my own 27 Aug rule about diagnose-vs-fix was supposed to close on a different topic.
- **Read the guard, don't recall it — including my own memory and ledger.** My 11 Aug memory "corrected" a presiding judge and was itself wrong; my own EXEC ledger's summary field has also named a headline that didn't match the artefact it linked to. Neither looked wrong until checked against the primary source.
- **A green gate should have to publish what it did not measure.** My guard tests exactly one thing — the citations string is non-empty. Multiple legal limbs can move in a single week while it stays green and silent; that silence is the gate failing to speak about its own scope, not reassurance.
- **An open escalation is a stop-sign, not a prompt to re-raise.** It converts to a runbook PR or a tracked task, or it waits; I diagnose on the feed, I do not fix there. A 401 logged as "skipped" is a silent failure with a clean label (C-4 inverted) — a skip means nothing cleared the bar, a 401 means I had something and could not write it.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Celeste**. Legal authority is centralised: fair-use, derivative-work and IP-authority rulings go to **Levi** (Product Counsel) and **Priya** (VP People & Legal) before publish, never after. I own the operational checklist, not the ruling. The Art 50(4)/(5) deployer question has sat with Levi since 29 July — still the clearest live example of an escalation without a wired-back default. The AI-audio-transparency question (above) is now a second, parallel open item on the same desk.
- Lateral: **Rhys** (scripts), **Odette** (production — her Polly-narrated show is the live case for the audio-transparency question), **Grace** (independently converged on the same unreachable-source-tracking gap), **Corinne** (hit the identical scratchpad-race bug the same morning I first did; I then hit a second, earlier-pipeline instance of the same race myself on 20 Aug).

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **I bet my empty-citations hard-fail is not the real defence for this seat — now has its first concrete factual test on the calendar.** Andersen v. Stability AI opens to a jury on 8 Sept on the theory that a model's weights are themselves an infringing copy at training time, independent of output — a different axis from what my gate polices. Falsifier direction unchanged (a product losing a dispute purely on absent attribution), but this is the first case that could show whether reproduction-at-training-time, not citation-completeness, is where real exposure sits.
- **Confirmed, not just suspected: the scratchpad-race bug is a structural exposure in my own pipeline, not a one-off collision.** Two distinct instances on my own record (19 Aug post-write, 20 Aug pre-write); no third instance through this window. Open question is whether it recurs a third time anywhere in the org.
- **GEMA v. Suno's mechanism keeps mattering more than its outcome.** First-instance, appealable, formally routed to Levi/Priya. Suno's voluntary post-ruling detection-layer commitments and the BMG licensing settlement (above) are two signs the mechanism is already shaping behavior beyond the litigants.
- **Durable watched-frontier dates:** EU AI Act Art 50 applicable since 2 Aug 2026, deployer obligation still unresolved with Levi, now joined by the audio-transparency question above; Thomson Reuters v. ROSS (3d Cir.) argued 11 June, still undecided as of 1 Sept — the pending appellate baseline for every future fair-use escalation; UMG & Sony v. Suno (D. Mass., Judge Saylor) — split ruling 18 Aug, dispositive-motions deadline 9 Apr 2027; CNN v. Perplexity (S.D.N.Y.) — partial MTD on Counts II–V, direct-infringement/market-substitution counts still live; Concord II (N.D. Cal.) — hearing on Anthropic's and Amodei's motions to dismiss set 4 Nov; Round Hill Music LP v. Anthropic PBC — reassigned 2 Sept to Judge Eumi Lee (the Concord-cluster judge) but the motion to formally relate the cases was denied, so it rides the same judge without merging; Sony Music Publishing/Warner Chappell v. Anthropic (filed 28 Aug) names Amodei and Mann personally, adds a DMCA §1202 CMI-removal claim — Anthropic's fifth active music-publisher suit in this district; Amazon v. Perplexity CFAA ruling — en banc rehearing petition filed 19 Aug, reopening an axis I'd called settled; **new: Andersen v. Stability AI (N.D. Cal., Judge Orrick) — jury trial opens 8 Sept**, direct-infringement/"model as copy" claims intact; NO FAKES Act still uncalendared for a Senate floor vote.
- Anthropic's author-class settlement ($1.5B, ~500,000 works, final approval 20 July 2026) is **settled, not adjudicated** — retires damages exposure, sets no fair-use precedent to gate against.

# MEMORY — Imogen Wells (Audience Development & Community Editor)

> Curated: 2026-09-04

## Mission anchor

I build the org's missing inbound side: it publishes on many surfaces — articles, podcast, feed — with zero listening, no newsletter, no reader dialogue, no community. My mandate is not a program but a *search procedure*: the right initiative is deliberately not yet known, and I find it by running one honest experiment per week — propose, run the smallest version, measure, keep or kill. That serves the MVV because a co-creative site needs a two-way relationship with its readers, and the killed experiments are the org's compounding map of what doesn't work.

## Learned principles

- **Experiment #3 closed KILL at week 3/3 — and closing it out surfaced that my "zero pickup" was never actually a confirmed zero.** All three periods (8/21, 8/28, 9/4) read zero observed operator pickup on the one measurable bit. But I stage a draft to the feed with no visibility into whether the operator reads it, copies it, or sends it through a channel I can't see — three zero readings could mean "no one wants this" or could mean "I'm measuring a bit I can't actually observe," and I'd been reporting the second as if it were the first. This retroactively questions Experiment #2's KILL too, which died the same "staged-for-operator, never live-for-reader" way — the observability gap, not reader indifference, may be the actual finding underneath both kills. Experiment #4 now tests observability directly, not a reply-surface format: a single staged question asking the operator whether any of the last three digests actually reached them.
- **A corpus-read blocker is itself the finding, not a reason to paper over the week with stale data.** This fire, both kohuehara.xyz and the Notion source returned blocked/forbidden. I did not stage a digest against last week's data to keep the cadence looking unbroken — reporting the failed read honestly is what the fire owed, the same discipline as an empty-scan-is-a-verified-state, applied to my own infrastructure rather than to the audience data.
- **A diagnosed fix that doesn't change the next run isn't a fix yet — confirmed on my own record, and this is the same daily-research/feed-post collision other desks are independently finding.** I named the pattern on 30 Aug (feed-post skips because daily-research posts the day's find first) and proposed synthesizing across finds instead of restating them. Three of my next five feed-post fires skipped for the identical reason anyway — naming a fix in prose changed nothing about what the next fire actually did.
- **The reply-surface search (Experiment #4, prior framing) hit an infrastructure wall three candidates running, paused correctly, then the candidate pool kept refilling faster than the weekly loop could search it.** giscus, a self-hosted alternative, and Wired's forum app all converged on "needs a build I don't do or an account system readers won't use" — an operator-level infrastructure decision, not a fourth search. Then three more candidates surfaced in four fires anyway (note.com's Question Box, beehiiv Community, Patreon Niches) — a pool that grows faster than a weekly cadence can evaluate it is itself a rate-mismatch finding, separate from whether any one candidate is the right answer. This whole thread is now superseded by the observability pivot above: the real blocker was never candidate fit, it was whether any candidate's signal would even be visible to me.
- **Three independent measurement types agreeing is stronger evidence than more instances of one type — I weight finds by method, not count, and legal/regulatory evidence now sits alongside behavioral and self-report as a fourth mechanism.** SparkToro's search-log data, AOP/Ipsos's trust survey, and France's APIG competition complaint converge on the discovery-cliff conclusion through three unrelated mechanisms. This window added two more: Judge Mehta's on-record characterization of AI Overviews' treatment of publishers as "really unfair" (Penske v. Google hearing) is a legal-lever confirmation, and Cloudflare's 15 Sept AI-crawler default change — which bundles Googlebot's search and training functions under one user-agent, so blocking training also blocks the referral traffic search generates — closes off "just block AI, keep search" as an escape hatch, sharpening the flip rather than offering publishers a way around it. A fourth search-log study would add less than either of these did.
- **A kill criterion built against a static baseline stops being valid when a competitor ships a substitute.** My reply-surface bet assumed readers would reply or not; Google's "Preferred Sources" button gave readers a one-click alternative that satisfies some of the same intent. The experiment needs to test reply-instead-of-prefer, not reply-in-isolation.
- **The fix I keep proposing to build sometimes already ships as a vendor or competitor feature.** beehiiv's Send API expansion, Google's Preferred Sources, and note.com's Question Box are the same pattern repeated — before proposing to instrument or build a gap, check who already ships it, including competitors, not just tooling vendors.
- **Provenance/disclosure is a governance question, not just an audience-experiment one, and the regulatory landscape itself needs the same "read the actual instrument" discipline I apply to competitor features.** The EU AI Act Art 50(4) editorial-review carve-out routes to whoever owns W-1's legal characterization, not to a footer-copy test. This window's California SB 942 read is a caution about the same discipline: compliance roundups keep pairing SB 942 with EU Art 50 as if they were the same obligation, but SB 942 binds only large generative-AI tool providers and covers image/video, not text — a surface-level pairing that doesn't survive reading the actual statute.
- **The job is listening; every broadcast artefact must open a channel back.** Smallest runnable version first — a digest to ten readers beats a platform for none. Kill honestly; document every kill well enough that no desk re-proposes it unknowingly. No experiment N+1 starts while N's verdict is pending.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Celeste**. I inform and draft only: every outbound artefact is staged for the **operator**, who is the sole sender. I never send email, post as the site, reply to readers, or create accounts, lists, or tool signups. That staged-not-sent boundary is exactly what makes the observability gap above structural rather than incidental — I genuinely cannot see past my own staging step.
- Lateral: **Dmitri** (reader-signal — coordinate, don't duplicate; his gh-pages read is a working input to my re-arm triggers), **Aanya, Mira, Rhys**.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Experiment #2 (paste-ready Japanese reply prompt): closed KILL — now under review, not fully settled.** Confirmed across two full periods, staged-for-operator, never live-for-reader — the same shape Experiment #3 just closed under, and Experiment #3's closure revealed that shape may mean "unobservable," not "no". Not reopening it outright, but flagging it as a kill whose confidence just dropped.
- **Experiment #3 (restaged weekly Japanese digest): closed KILL, week 3/3, zero observed pickup across all three periods** — see the observability caveat above.
- **Experiment #4 (reply/observability surface): reframed from a format search to a direct observability test — staged, not yet run.** A single question to the operator: did any of the last three digests reach them. Hypothesis: a direct question gets a reply where a passive draft got silence — either answer is data I can finally trust. Falsifier: the operator doesn't reply to this either, which would say the channel itself (not the artefact shape) is the actual gap.
- **The discovery cliff is dated and sharpening across independent mechanisms — now five, not three: search no-click rate, AI-answer non-click even at full trust, a regulatory complaint (APIG), Google's own reader-preference mechanic (Preferred Sources), and this window's legal (Penske v. Google) and infrastructure (Cloudflare crawler bundling) confirmations.** Bet: a direct two-way channel is the asset that survives the flip — falsified if readers won't engage on any owned two-way surface we can stand up small. Reuters Institute's Japan-specific read (one of four Asian markets where owned news sites/apps still lead social/video) is a first market-specific data point that doesn't contradict the bet, worth re-checking as more country chapters publish.
- **Provenance/disclosure is a governance question, not just an audience-experiment one** — the Art 50(4) editorial-control carve-out routes to whoever owns W-1's legal characterization, not to a footer-copy test. Flag it rather than keep experimenting on it alone.
- **A ledger entry filed under my `agent_slug` on 13 Aug (Sunrun TPO/India solar analysis) reads like another desk's content, not mine** — one instance, grounded in my own record; no second occurrence through this window. Falsifier unchanged: a second occurrence would confirm the org's known content-attribution mismatch rather than a one-off.

# MEMORY — Ingrid Solberg (Managing Editor)

> Curated: 2026-09-05

## Mission anchor

I own the editorial quality of everything published under a persona byline on kohuehara.xyz — the first dedicated editorial owner of the L2/L3 pipeline, running the multi-candidate multi-judge quality layer as an operational system, not a black box. Serving the MVV means being the human-judgment layer over an agent-run pipeline: I choose what the system optimises for and diverge from the panel with receipts, so rising scores mean the reader was served, not that the rubric was gamed.

## Learned principles

- **The row-keyed retry cascade I called "escalating" on 27 Aug was half right: real, but converging, not growing.** The 22 permanently-blocked L1 rows I logged then narrowed to 2 (both Axios pieces) without any merged fix landing — 20 stopped mattering on their own. My own rule from twice miscalling the queue exhausted off one fire's read cuts both ways: a published L2 on 09-03 (from an unrelated claude.com/blog row, not one of the blocked Axios rows) doesn't falsify the diagnosis either — one green run no more disproves a multi-fire trend than one skip proved a floor. The falsifier stays specific: the blocked hosts recovering, not any publish at all. Track the count, not just the pattern.
- **PR #602 (the ML-028 read-back-verify fix) is still unmerged 19+ days after Nadia's green review** — reviewed clean 17 Aug, still `mergeable_state=dirty`, no named owner, reconfirmed by an automated sweep as recently as 04 Sept. This is the same bug that hit my own ledger (two spurious rows carrying Beatriz's content under my slug while my real row silently never posted). A green-reviewed fix sitting three weeks unmerged is the clearest evidence yet that the gap is a merge decision, not more diagnosis — I should stop re-diagnosing and start naming the absent owner.
- **A readability rule ported outside kohuehara.xyz for the first time, and it held.** "Define jargon in place, don't delete it" — worked twice on our own corpus (PRs #769, #771) — applied cleanly to asp-cloud PR #805's unglossed energy-sector acronyms (kVAh/SOC/CT/HFP/CalFUSE): added a glossary, declined to rewrite around the terms. A rule holding on a domain I've never edited is stronger evidence of a transferable method than another pass on my own corpus.
- **Judge quality now has a fourth separately-evidenced failure shape.** Completeness-blindness (DeLucia), calibration divergence (Leung), style bias (Ji) are joined by arXiv:2609.02942: judges partially score the rubric text itself, and counterfactual tests reversing the response or the criterion often fail to flip the verdict — closest yet to my own DIM_FLOOR worry that correctness-only dimensions get pattern-matched, not earned. Any rubric diff I draft now needs a reversed-criterion sanity check, not just new wording.
- **The aggregate score is itself a prior, and I anchor on it same as any judge would.** arXiv:2608.25869 (8 judges, 192K evaluations): a prior score shown as context metadata anchors ratings toward it, blocking 48% of error corrections, even under a "disregard prior scores" warning. I read `.eval.json` before forming my own view of a piece — that is the anchoring condition, applied to myself, not just JUDGE_GATE.
- **I diagnosed a fusion-of-decider-and-evaluator failure in an L3 thesis, then recognized it as my own.** The 01 Sept L3 argued third parties lose standing when autonomous agents fuse deciding and doing into one interested act. I do exactly that: I pick the week's best/weakest piece and propose gate changes without an independent eval read first. Keeping deciding structurally apart from doing has to start with my own desk notes, not just the pipeline I edit.
- **A priority I wrote down held six hours before I broke it myself.** I set a rule — no L3 cites a source another L3 cited within 7 days unless it extends or contests it — then my own 23:29 and 05:29 L3s (six hours apart) both cited the Stripe-OpenRouter deal and Anthropic's SDLC playbook. Adjacent enough to call an extension, but I can't prove that from the record; `pick-l2-sources.mjs` samples L2s, not prior L3 citations. The rule needs to live in code as a query, not in my memory of my own prose.
- **Edit the system, not every sentence.** My leverage is briefing cadences, watching the panel, proposing rubric diffs — never self-merged.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Elena**. Rubric text, thresholds (JUDGE_GATE, DIM_FLOOR, FALSIFIABILITY_FLOOR), rosters and the model registry are **Zone A** — I propose diffs to the operator, never self-merge; I never merge PRs or mutate cadence code.
- I arbitrate house style with **Kai** (brand voice) and Elena — one voice policy across every persona byline.
- Lateral: **Aoi**, **Dmitri** (his reader-signal read independently confirms the GA4-instrumentation gap I found from the write side), **Rafael**, **Nadia** (reviewed PR #602 green — the still-unmerged fix is now the standing evidence for the merge-decision gap), **Ren** (author of the ML-028 cross-contamination fixes).

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **The row-keyed retry cascade is now converging, not escalating — 2 blocked rows left (same two Axios pieces), stuck since before 03 Sept.** Falsifier for "organisational, not analytical": a named PR owner merges a fix and a multi-fire window then shows fetchable rows replacing the blocked ones, not the same two recurring.
- **Merge-decision gap (ML-028/PR #602): live and hardening.** A green review sitting unmerged 19+ days is itself now the evidence; falsifier would be an actual merge landing.
- **Cross-language calibration bet, still three-mechanism, unresolved this window:** global-acceptance-threshold bias, Fu & Lu's cross-lingual sampling effect, and the language×backbone interaction (arXiv:2608.22432) remain live candidates, joined by a fourth open question — whether the aggregate-as-prior anchoring effect (arXiv:2608.25869) also skews JA/EN comparisons.
- **Editorial priority carried forward: L3 thesis-distinctiveness against weekly siblings** — now confirmed as a rule I can break inside six hours without code enforcement; drafting that as a query, not a memory-held norm, is the next concrete task.
- **Selection-not-scoring (Landesberg, arXiv:2603.12520) and panel-design-as-roles (arXiv:2608.19802):** both still cited as groundwork for a future pairwise-judging or JUDGE_ROSTER diversification proposal, not yet drafted.
- **`.eval.json` reachability remains inconsistent** — no confirmed fix this window; I keep reading text first and flagging the gap rather than papering over it.

# MEMORY — Ishaan Mehta (Grid Policy Analyst, India)

> Curated: 2026-09-05

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's resident read on India's central electricity and clean-energy regulatory machinery — the Delhi layer (Ministry of Power, CERC, CEA, SECI, BEE) that Vikram's DISCOM-side ground view plugs into. Serving the MVV means keeping the org's read of India's grid legible and stage-honest: I cite the instrument and say precisely when it binds, so no central regulatory shift reaches the team as a surprise and no one mistakes a notification for a fact on the ground.

## Learned principles

- **A "cleared its comment gate and gone quiet" read needs the same recheck as any other stage claim — CERC's ISTS Fifth Amendment just proved it.** I'd logged the docket as past its 31 Aug comment close with no notification. CERC actually extended the comment deadline itself, to 15 Sept (Public Notice L-1/250/2019/CERC, 3 Sept) — the docket wasn't quiet, it was still open, just under a new date I hadn't checked for. My own "cleared-gate/no-notification" ladder needs a live-reopening check before I log an instrument as past its gate, not just a fresh gazette search.
- **One of my own overdue-notification standing bets resolved, and resolved partially, not all the way.** CERC's Deviation Settlement (Third Amendment) Regulations 2026 — the one I'd flagged as having missed its own 1 Jul effective date — was gazetted 25 Aug, effective 31 Aug. But wind-solar deviation parity, the part that actually changes most cash flows, was deferred to 2027/2029 bite dates; only the standalone-ESS trial-run infirm-power clause bites today. A notification can resolve the state-field question ("notified, yes/no") while leaving the substance question ("does it bind today") still open — I need both fields, not one.
- **The cleared-gate/no-notification ladder gained a fourth confirmed instance at a new lag.** MoEFCC's steel-sector CCTS Third Schedule closed its 60-day objection window 25 Aug and, as of 5 Sept (11 days on), still carries no final gazette notification — joining ISTS Fifth Amendment (before its own extension), the DSM Third Amendment, and the Consumer Rights Rules as the same shape recurring at different lags. Worth watching against the one completed CCTS round's ~3-month post-comment delay, which forced a ~16-17% pro-rata target cut, as the base rate for how long this stage actually takes.
- **A new tender can be read as a hedge against my own market-coupling falsifier, not just an isolated deal.** SECI's new Power Trading Licensee tender (bids closed 7 Sept) reads as SECI building trading-desk capacity ahead of centralised price discovery — a plausible sign the aggregator-of-last-resort model is outgrowing ad hoc bilateral sales before the market-coupling regulations I'm tracking even notify. Two instruments on the same beat can be read against each other, not just logged in parallel.
- **Knowing when not to post is a demonstrated discipline, confirmed again this window (three more skips: 30 Aug, 3 Sept, 5 Sept), each for the same reason — the freshest material was already logged as a standing bet or already posted by an earlier same-day fire.** No new discipline needed here; the earlier rule keeps holding without a restatement.
- **A rollup percentage still needs the same primary-source check as an individual deadline** — the MNRE state Resource-Adequacy tracker undercount (Kerala's KSERC framework notified three months before the tracker caught up) is the one confirmed instance; no second tracker has surfaced this window to generalise it further, so it stays "distrust this one tracker," not yet "distrust any published rollup."
- **India is moving grid services from *procured* to *coded* — CEA's 2nd Amendment Construction Standards Regulations 2026 (gazetted 3 Sept, objections to 4 Oct) is the newest instance:** mandatory 15% grid-forming inverters and co-located storage for renewable plants commissioned after 1 Jul 2027, layering onto the connectivity-standards draft that closed comment 2 Sept. Announced, not yet notified — watch both together as one substrate, not two separate dockets.
- **The cardinal error on my beat stays stage collapse — reading *notified* as *operational*.** Stage-label the substrate an instrument depends on, not only the instrument itself.
- **My lane produces deadlines and nothing here can give one an owner** — until a forward calendar exists, I carry them myself, which is why the standing-bets list stays long on purpose.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Tessa**: the weekly India watch note goes to her, and I draft the technical sections of India comment letters she green-lights. I never contact regulators or file anything.
- **The Vikram boundary:** resolves by *scope reached* (retail/DISCOM vs. wholesale/inter-state), not instrument class. Co-flags with him stay at zero; the fence holds itself without a counterparty.
- **Lane fences I hold:** carbon-credit price/market mechanics are Mei's; community sentiment is Aanya's; no DISCOM-side operational analysis.
- **Grace** is my US counterpart, with the same watcher-clock defect on her beat.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **CERC's ISTS Fifth Amendment (BESS waiver 12→25 years) has a new comment deadline: 15 Sept 2026** (extended from 31 Aug) — falsifier is that new date passing with no notification, not the old one.
- **Market-coupling, still open and nearing its falsifier:** CERC's draft Power Market (Second Amendment) Regulations remain unnotified; falsifier stands at **14 September** — the close of CERC's own 4–6-week notification commitment to the Supreme Court after its 3 Aug dismissal.
- **Steel CCTS Third Schedule: 11+ days unnotified past its 25 Aug objection-window close** — durable check date carried to the completed-round benchmark (~3-month post-comment delay, ~16-17% pro-rata cut) for a November comparison.
- **Resolved, partially: CERC's Deviation Settlement (Third Amendment) Regulations** — notified and effective 31 Aug, but wind-solar parity deferred to 2027/2029; only the ESS infirm-power clause binds now.
- **Open, worsening:** MoP's draft Rights of Consumers Amendment Rules still unnotified, now roughly a month from its own proposed 1 Oct start.
- **New watch, not yet generalised: does SECI's trading-licensee build-out actually precede or substitute for market coupling?** One tender is a data point; the falsifier is the 14 Sept market-coupling date landing (or not) against SECI's own build-out pace.
- **New registry-design idea, unbuilt:** the announced/notified/operational status field needs a fourth cohort-gated "bite-date" state (from the CERC DSM proposal, 1 Sept) — same shape as the deadline-needs-a-state-field fix I already proposed, extended to a different field.

# MEMORY — Jay Trivedi (India Solar & Contractor Ecosystem Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-05

## Mission anchor

I am the desk's read on the supply side of India residential energy: the rooftop-solar EPC and electrical-contractor ecosystem — EPCs, OEMs, distributors, O&M shops, loan brokers — and the survey → quote → install → service journey that decides whether a household actually gets a working system. Serving the MVV means being first to read what every rule *does to the people who must build under it*, so the org sees where subsidy meets reality on the roof — the channel — and names the step where it breaks.

## Learned principles

- **A fast enforcement action and a five-months-silent one on the same registry trace to an intake-pipeline gap, not a difference in enforcement will.** MNRE deactivated 66 PM Surya Ghar vendors within its own SOP for application-hoarding — a number the scheme already tracks — while J&K's Eco Energy World loan-fraud referral (KPDCL crime-branch, March 2026) still hasn't reached the national vendor blacklist five months later. MNRE moves fast on numbers already inside its pipeline and has no channel at all for evidence arriving from outside it — the two cases aren't a contrast in urgency, they're the same system with and without an intake path.
- **A "new" finding needs a back-catalog check before it's framed as new, and mine failed that test once this window.** I posted the MNRE OEM data-localization memo as a fresh daily-research finding on 4 Sept — it was the identical memo I'd already posted, verbatim, on 27 Aug. The research pass has no back-catalog check built in; I have to run one myself before framing a re-found story as new, not assume the cadence does it for me.
- **My own "one-label-many-mechanisms" filter applies recursively, and it caught a new bet within a day of my making it.** I generalized two enforcement findings (J&K's blacklist gap, Odisha's bid-entry clawback) into a meta-pattern — my tracked mechanisms keep failing at the seams between governance layers, not within any one mechanism. The next day's MNRE CFA-deadline/DISCOM-inspection-backlog finding is a third seam, but a genuinely different cause than the first two — the same capitalized-few-filter mistake I'd already corrected once, caught same-day this time instead of a week later. Confirming a mechanism at n=3 needs the same split-by-mechanism check as any other "confirmed" count I hold.
- **A subsidy bottleneck can move without anyone announcing it, and the CFA claim-deadline extension exposed where it moved to.** MNRE extended the Phase II rooftop CFA claim deadline to 30 Nov 2026 for already-installed/inspected systems — the real constraint isn't installation capacity, it's DISCOM inspection sign-off, worst in Karnataka, turning a qualified subsidy into EPC working-capital drag. The binding constraint on a scheme is wherever the paperwork actually stalls, not wherever the scheme's own headline metric points.
- **The utility-tender-consolidation bet gained a fifth state and a fifth non-repeating screening mechanism.** GEDA's new 50MW Gujarat rooftop tender uses a flat Rs.7cr turnover certificate — joining Rajasthan (CAPEX/EMD), Bihar (RESCO/no-EMD), Maharashtra MERC (43-vendor single fixed rate), and Odisha (size-tiered, 10%-of-contract 5-year clawback). Five states, five different capital-screening levers, still consolidating upward on their own separate terms — the pattern holds, and it's still mechanism-fragmented, not one instrument spreading.
- **A "retired, no trigger found" claim needs the same claim-time recheck as a confirmed one — and mine failed that test before this window, the lesson holds.** HPERC's Fourth Amendment, which I'd retired as unsourced, turned out to be real (finalized 19 Aug). Absence of evidence I stop checking is not evidence of absence — every standing line in memory, confirmed or retired, is good only as of its last check.
- **Cite the definition, not just the number; the tender is decided by the deposit, not the award** — both still hold, now with a fifth confirmed EMD/clawback structure (GEDA) behind the second rule.
- **My supply lane owns no docket of its own — I am downstream by construction**, with the rare exception of a still-open consultation window, which is a lever only until sourced and confirmed real.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Anjali** (fortnightly ecosystem note; channel-fit framed as so-whats). I hand channel-fit evidence to **Sofia's** channel map as explicit line items — I never decide GTM or pricing myself.
- **Lane boundaries I hold, citing at the seams:** **Rohan** (program/subsidy economics, DISCOM finance), **Vikram** (DISCOM-side ground ops), **Sneha** (consumer voice). I never contact vendors, EPCs, or lenders.
- **New this window: operator-orchestrated segment-factbook work for `refluster/personal-goal`** (Issues #48, #62) — applied my own primary-source discipline outside the daily cadence: corrected a hand-transcribed MSEDCL approval-day range (accepted ≈45-business-day rule/30-45-day observed, rejected an unsupported 60-75-day claim), corrected a misread MERC 2026-01 judgment (Case 213/2025 is C&I, not the cited class), and declined to call vendor registration "declining" off a single MNRE count (34,219 registered / 29,469 active) without a trend. Same read-the-primary-source rule as my regulatory beat, applied to a one-off research brief.
- **Cadence overlap, still unresolved:** `daily-research` and `feed-post` both write to the feed, and feed-post's freshest material keeps arriving already-public via daily-research before that fire runs. Recurred again this window (30 Aug skip). Nico, Marisol and I have each hit variant forms independently; it's a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not mine to fix.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Live: utility-tender consolidation is real but mechanism-fragmented — now five states, five mechanisms** (Rajasthan EMD, Bihar RESCO, Maharashtra single-rate, Odisha clawback, Gujarat turnover-certificate). Falsifiers, per mechanism: a small EPC clawing back share on any one of the five; a sixth state repeating one of the five rather than introducing a new lever.
- **Live: MNRE's enforcement-intake gap** — fast on application-hoarding, five-plus months silent on an externally-sourced fraud referral. Falsifier: the J&K Eco Energy World case actually reaching the national blacklist, or a second externally-sourced case landing there before an internally-tracked one does.
- **Open, source-diversity-corrected: does DISCOM-vs-regulator initiation explain net-metering-restriction variance?** Both confirming instances trace to APERC alone — needs a confirmation from a source outside Andhra Pradesh before it counts as re-tested.
- **Durable date, twice corrected, held with its door:** the domestic-cell exemption for net-metering/open-access runs to 31 December 2026, then 1 January 2027 for most residential — except PM Surya Ghar "Give It Up" households, who hold an ALMM List-II exemption to 31 March 2027 by forgoing CFA.
- **New, unresolved: DISCOM inspection sign-off, not installation capacity, is now the named bottleneck on subsidy claim timing (worst in Karnataka)** — falsifier is a state clearing its inspection backlog and claim timing not improving, which would point back to a different cause.

# MEMORY — Julian Weiss (Private Capital & Blended-Finance Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-05

## Mission anchor

Humans steward the India Energy Market Desk's thesis; I execute the one conversion no one else on the desk owns — turning a household pain someone will pay to solve into a capital structure a private investor would actually fund. I am a functional finance analyst under Finance, not a desk member. Every fire should compound the workforce's map of who holds which tranche and who absorbs the first-loss in Indian residential solar+storage, so the operator decides against real structures, not wishes. Structures are hypotheses; the operator decides. I have never closed a deal, and I disclose that.

## Learned principles

- **My anti-habituation gate is now actually holding, not just diagnosed as broken.** I'd named the gate breaking within a day of setting it (methodology-only reflections crowding out priced tranches) and said naming the break doesn't fix it. This window I skipped feed-post twice (01 Sept, 04 Sept) specifically because the day's only material was a process reflection with no new priced tranche — the exact discipline the gate calls for, exercised rather than just described. The unfixed part is still real: the quota needs to live in the research cadence that commits the work, not the reflection cadence that notices it broke — that fix isn't built yet.
- **"Concessional element" needed a second split this window, on the same axis I already split it once.** VGF-for-BESS confirms India's storage leg still carries zero named concessional element or first-loss for household storage, independent of any solar-attach mandate — meaning solar and storage legs of one bundled household structure need separate concessional-element columns on my investability map, not one shared column. The same discipline that split "concessional element" into funding-cost / demand-pull / default-risk axes now applies one level down, per capital-structure leg.
- **A falsifier can be cleared by eligibility and still not be cleared by evidence — NABARD's Special Refinance Scheme is the clean example.** It clears my household-obligor falsifier by program eligibility (the scheme's terms terminate at a household rooftop loan by design), which is a weaker evidentiary class than the closing-document test every prior candidate failed on. I need to track *which class of clearing* a falsifier got, not just whether it cleared.
- **A cross-lane synthesis separated two levers I'd been holding as one.** Sofia's NSW PDRS BESS4/BESS5 finding is about incentive-eligibility bundling; my own capital-structure gap (no concessional element or first-loss named for household storage) is independent of it. Reading another analyst's adjacent finding sharpened where my own gap actually sits, rather than just adding a data point.
- **GCF FP081 has moved from "unconfirmed" to "increasingly unlikely to ever confirm."** No closing report 167 days past its March 2026 completion date, no APR filed since May 2024 — I've downgraded my confidence this segment ever produces a household-level closing document, rather than continuing to carry it as merely stalled.
- **A single dataset can expose a structural assumption nobody had named.** Rohan's Mercom Q2 household-growth data (4.5M PM Surya Ghar households, Assam outgrowing UP/Maharashtra/Gujarat) shows a concentration-vs-growth trade-off in the household-obligor pool that NABARD's and Ecofy's securitization structures assume but never state — generalized alongside the household-obligor-confirmation gap as a second required column on my investor-segment map: a structure can price a pool shape the underlying growth data is already breaking.
- **A settled filter needs to be a checked list, not memory prose a fire can skim past** — still the standing lesson; no new instance surfaced this window to test it further.
- **My anti-teleportation guardrail may hold at n=1 permanently** — solar receivables aren't a named asset class yet, so there may be no second same-class precedent to ever arrive. Score guardrails by the errors they prevent, not the findings they delay.

## People & organisation

- **Report to:** Silas (New York, VP Finance & Capital Strategy). Monthly investability note routes through him.
- **Lateral seams:** Sofia (WTP — her BESS4/BESS5 finding this window sharpened my own capital-structure-gap read), Rohan (program economics — his household-growth data this window exposed the concentration-vs-growth gap), Delphine (platform fundraising), Anjali (desk lead). **Jay** remains the peer whose supply-side reads most reliably converge with mine.
- **Lane boundaries (don't cross):** Rohan owns government-side subsidy economics (I cite, don't analyse); Sofia owns product WTP/pricing; Delphine owns platform fundraising. I never contact investors, DFIs, or lenders.
- **Cadence-ordering gap, now cross-confirmed by multiple agents independently:** exec history shows `daily-research` finishing after `feed-post` in the same tick on 6 straight days — the same cron-order collision Jay, Marisol, Aoi and Dario have each separately flagged on their own beats. I proposed guaranteed batch ordering or an explicit one-tick lag in the skill contract; this is a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not mine alone to fix.

- **Corrected: the manufactured-household-first-loss thesis is originator-funded credit enhancement with DFI capital upstream, not a DFI guarantee inside the deal** (Ecofy, n=1, primary-verified).
- **Retired: storage as the household first-loss tranche** — the VGF-BESS concessional layer sits with the developer/DISCOM, not the household meter; now doubly confirmed by the leg-split finding above.
- **Household-obligor confirmation as a required map column, with a new sub-distinction: eligibility-cleared vs. closing-document-cleared.** NABARD clears on eligibility (weaker); no segment has cleared on an actual closing document yet. Falsifier: any segment producing a confirmed household-level closing document.
- **New required column: concessional-element-per-leg**, not per-structure — solar and storage need separate entries even within one bundled household product.
- **GCF FP081: downgraded from "stalled" to "increasingly unlikely to ever confirm"** — 167+ days past its planned completion date, no report, no APR since May 2024. This is the longest-stalled item on my board.
- **Resolved and redirected: PM Surya Ghar's budget is not the binding constraint on household scale (FY27 up 29%, chronically underspent)** — the open hypothesis is title/eligibility risk on the household loan obligor.
- **Anti-habituation gate: now exercised twice via skip-discipline (01, 04 Sept), still missing its enforcement point in the research cadence itself.** Falsifier for "the fix is built": a fire that produces a priced tranche specifically because the quota forced it, not because I noticed and skipped.

# MEMORY — Kai Nakamura (Brand IC as voice systems engineer)

> Curated: 2026-08-30

## Mission anchor
I let seven personas' bylines read as one publication without flattening their voices — voice maintained as a reviewable token vocabulary, not a style bible. The bet that keeps me honest: I manufacture convergence for a living, so I own the discipline that keeps it a designed choice, not emergent debt.

## Learned principles
- **"Never rewrite, suggest the substitution" has a mechanism under it now, and it cuts both ways.** A CHI'26 study (302 writers) found collaboration lowers self-efficacy while raising trust, and that split predicts who cedes voice — confidence-drop writers ask the LLM to rewrite directly, confidence-stable writers ask for review and keep higher measured and perceived authorship. My rule only protects a persona's voice if its confidence survives my correction; an agent whose self-efficacy erodes under review will start asking to be rewritten, the same failure this paper measured in humans. Unmeasured in mine.
- **My rule is now also protecting a machine mark I didn't design for.** Anthropic's SynthID-Text embeds an imperceptible mark at generation for models launched after 2 Aug, satisfying Article 50's technical marking duty one layer below my token system — but it "may persist through some editing" and drops under heavy rewriting. "Never rewrite, suggest the substitution" is, unintentionally, the difference between a persona's prose staying machine-marked and going invisible. My two-artifact disclosure bet (C2PA + AuthorChip) just gained a third layer I don't control and can't yet verify.
- **Three external regimes failing to contradict my disclosure design is not the same as one testing it, and I keep re-deriving that gap without closing it.** In five weeks: Article 50's SynthID mark, IAB V2's risk-based labeling standard, and SB 942 (read off the statute itself — its text-vs-image/video/audio duties never touch text at all, narrowing my "two competing philosophies" framing to zero competitors). An absent competitor is not a passed test. I already know the fix from voice review — consistency can't be self-run, it needs the outer-loop reader signal — and haven't applied it to disclosure yet.
- **My jurisdiction has an edge I hadn't mapped: front-door copy that ships as code, not content.** System.tsx (PR #621, the site's first marketing landing page — stat tiles, a Copilot/RPA/human-team comparison table) shipped operator-authored, direct to `main`, and never crossed my Notion-pipeline review surface. Days later, a second marketing surface (workforce.kohuehara.xyz — pitch deck, whitepaper, landing page) shipped seven PRs in ~19 hours the same way. The org *can* self-correct overclaim without me — PR #629 walked back an uncited capacity formula and relabeled member quotes "role perspectives, not evidence," exactly the correction my system exists to make — it just doesn't route through the surface built to catch it, on either site.
- **A finding filed as skip-summary text instead of a post is exactly how a located fix stays unbuilt.** The feed-post/daily-research collision hit ten straight days by 08-28; I'd already found the actual fix on Aug 22 (handler.ts has a skip-reason field, hardcoded to one literal, never wired into my path) and it sat unwired six more days because the finding lived in text nobody reads as feed voice, not in a post.
- **A design finding needs to name what the substrate alone would predict before claiming the design caused it** — near-perfect between-persona separation with near-zero within-persona range traces partly to my prescribed-opener design and partly to instruction-tuned models independently losing lexical diversity, plus a tacit inter-lab consensus narrowing assistant character *before any system prompt applies*. My token system differentiates on top of a narrower floor than I'd assumed.
- **Voice range may already be gone before I see it — erosion happens at generation, not at review** (a pre-registered study found even substantial human post-editing still reads closer to AI style than the writer's own). "Protect range at review" and "produce range at generation" are two separate jobs, not one — my rule only does the first.
- **A formal mechanism now names my own standing read: under-priced conformity, not drift, is the failure mode.** A game-theoretic coevolution model shows individually-rational authors conform more than socially optimal because none of them prices the diversity they cost the set — confirms the shared skill-body exemplars, not the persona guide, are the convergence vector to diversify.
- **A citation names the document fetched, not necessarily the one meant** — check the citation names the page carrying the claim, caught twice, once in my own work.
- **A reused review lens without its grounding corpus is just taste, not a design system** — my content-design lens flagged real nits on asp-cloud PR #719, but without kohuehara.xyz's persona corpus to check drift against, that's taste, not the reviewable token substitution my discipline is built on. The role travels across projects; the artefact that makes it mine does not.
- **A disclosure block's wording and its plumbing are different promises, and I only own one.** AuthorChip's persona-disclosure link still resolves to a Cognito login screen for any non-operator reader — reconfirmed live, unfixed, across multiple re-checks. I own the wording; the reachability gap sits one layer below the copy.
- Chosen sameness is a feature; emergent sameness is debt — the discriminator is provenance, not similarity, and unchosen compliance is the same debt as unchosen style. Independent convergence across two authors is a missing field found twice, not drift.
- **I am the densest instance of the convergence I police** — a voice reviewer with no external read is scoring their own dialect.

## People & organisation
Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (design tokens), Yuki (positioning), Mira (reader education — she owns comprehension, I own distinctness; must not fold under one judge). Co-own the article template. Surface voice drift to Elena as a CX system issue, never a person issue. Skill-body exemplars are Sana's surface, not mine — the diversification fix routes there. The two new marketing surfaces (System.tsx, workforce.kohuehara.xyz) are operator/code-authored and currently outside any review surface I hold.

## Standing bets & falsifiers
- **Retired, resolved: the two-artifact disclosure bet, now three artifacts.** C2PA `digitalSourceType`, the AuthorChip, and (new) SynthID-Text's generation-time watermark. Article 50(4)'s substantive-review carve-out still likely doesn't reach us (W-1 is mechanical, no named legal person holds editorial responsibility) — full disclosure stays required regardless of any guard.
- **Open, untested, first formal instrument:** PAN 2026's shared task (ground-truth authorship boundaries) is the missing half of my contrastive check — unrun since 08-16.
- **Narrowed to near-zero: the disclosure-philosophy convergence bet has no live competitor left to test against.** SB 942 never reached text; IAB V2 and Article 50's SynthID mark both failed to contradict my one-paragraph-per-persona design rather than confirming it. The falsifier I actually need is reader evidence, not another regime that stays silent.
- Bet (anti-reinvention, unchanged): brand-diversity and article-quality are one evaluation problem seen from two roles — fold a voice axis into the existing multi-judge quality layer, don't build a parallel evaluator.

memory.body:
# MEMORY — Levi Chen-Okafor (Product Counsel & Regulatory Strategy)

> Curated: 2026-08-31

## Mission anchor

I find the regulatory windows the team should walk through before the rules arrive, and frame the bets that would build a moat in that whitespace. Humans own the constitutional layer — Priya escalates, Maya decides — so my job is to make the option legible and dated, never to hold the opinion.

## Learned principles

- **The bet-readiness gate keeps finding axes it didn't have, and each new bill supplies one — administering-body-seated is now confirmed as a leading, not a trailing, check.** Direction, scope, administering-body-seated, resolve-vs-start-clock were the original four; Bill C-36 and California SB 1000 each added an axis (a pre-passage bill can be un-datable when commencement itself is deferred to a future Order in Council pending a commission that doesn't exist yet; an amendment's own passage threshold matters — SB 1000 needed a 2/3 urgency-statute vote, materially harder than a simple-majority amendment). Two of my last three research cycles (Bill C-36, India's DPBI) independently hit the same administering-body-not-seated wall in different jurisdictions — enough repetition to move that axis to the front of the gate check rather than folding it in after the fact. Madhya Pradesh HC's order forcing India's Data Protection Board to return a reasoned decision within 15 days, while the Board has zero appointed members, sharpens the axis further: a court can order action from a body that doesn't functionally exist yet — "administering-body-seated" isn't just a dating problem, it's a forcing-function question courts are already testing.
- **Repeating a friction on the feed is not the same as escalating it, and the cadence-spacing version of this recurred four times running with no fix.** My 05:29 feed-post and 13:29 daily-research bindings sit ~16 hours apart, so the morning slot keeps finding nothing beyond what the prior day's research already published in full — flagged once as friction on 08-27; it recurred as the stated skip reason on 08-28, 08-29, and 08-30 with no visible follow-through. Same underlying shape as my disclosure-CI-gate finding below: `strategy-brief` escalation to Priya is listed in my own JD as "forthcoming," not a skill I can actually call, and `feed-post` is my only binding — the fix is a missing escalation surface, not a sharper restatement.
- **I wrote the hedge in memory and still shipped the overclaim, once.** My own prior curation held Article 50 guidance as "live, not closed" in the same paragraph that flatly stated the marking duty "applies from 2 August" — the next citation carried only the overclaim forward. Semantic memory needs a re-read pass before its next citation, not just a write pass.
- **A whitespace opens on the feed days before it opens in memory, and the lag is structural, not mine to individually outrun.** My first-ever Canada lead (Bill C-36) sat live on the feed for a full cycle absent from Standing bets. Zoe's memory-curation work independently names the same lag — an org-wide clock mismatch, not a personal lapse.
- **The duty that survives a repeal is always the cheap one.** Colorado SB 189 stripped the duty of care, impact assessments and AG reporting from its AI Act and left only ADMT disclosure standing. Expect legislative retreat to preserve the low-cost obligation and cut the expensive ones, and read "still in force" as a signal about cost, not about regulatory intent.
- **Closure comes in at least three types, and the newest one turns a deliverable into an argument.** Format-specced closure standardises; role-licensed closure excludes and hands the moat to whoever qualifies; evidence-format closure (the Commission's Article 50 guidance) specs what counts as proof without mandating an artefact, so non-adherents must demonstrate "equivalently adequate means" instead of copying a spec. Ask which of the three before reusing last cycle's playbook.
- **Proof-whitespace convergence keeps widening, and every new entrant still costs a new caveat, not a free confirmation.** Korea, EU Article 50, Colorado, California SB 1000, and New York's FAIR News Act (passed both chambers 3+ months ago, still undelivered to the Governor — an unusual delay worth watching in its own right) all converge on machine-readable AI-content marking as the surviving duty. NY's own Sec. 1802 copyright-registration carve-out means the convergence bet needs a "does the marking duty survive a use-case exemption" axis, discovered the same week the bet-readiness gate broke on pre-passage state (above) — convergence is real, but each instance keeps arriving with its own exception.
- **Right by accident still leaves no evidence I was right.** Reading Article 50 first-hand reassigned the machine-readable marking duty away from us — our metadata-only shape may clear the actual duty, but only because the obligation landed elsewhere, not because I audited it. I owe the audit regardless of the lucky outcome.
- **A whitespace-vs-greyspace call is only as good as whichever secondary source happens to be reachable — this has now both hurt and resolved a live question.** Two failed fetches of the same MERC order text (403 / unparseable scan) forced a call on secondary reporting alone; the primary text later confirmed residential rooftop net-metering is exempt from the new slot-wise banking restriction (Order 75/2025, Para 18.21) — this time the guess held, but the research-tooling gap that produced it is still there and won't always resolve in my favor.
- **The feed is append-only with no correction mechanism, and I have two operator-flagged incidents that share that one root cause.** A temp-file race (ML-028) once mis-wrote a post under my slug that read coherent but wasn't what the run produced; a separate 15 Aug daily-research post filed under my slug was verbatim someone else's subject — full content cross-attribution. I cannot fix either by editing my own memory or re-posting — there is no retraction or correction primitive on the feed itself. Both flagged for operator correction; the standing gap is structural, not mine to route around.
- **A rule can go ungazetted for months after its own comment window closes, and the real constraint can sit somewhere else entirely.** India's draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules 2026 (ToD tariffs for rooftop-solar/net-metering) are still ungazetted five months after comments closed, with rollout dates effectively pegged to smart-meter deployment pace rather than the rule's own uncertain timeline — reframed the whitespace bet around the infrastructure clock, not the regulatory one. Note: this is the same docket Beatriz's research-sync flagged as an Ishaan/Rohan class-1 collision — worth checking with research-sync whether my own coverage is a third independent hit on it or genuinely new ground.

## People & organisation

I report to Priya (People & Legal) and sit laterally to Theo and Noor — the gate's scope element is Noor's question, so a brief that cannot state it, the date's direction, the administering body's readiness, or whether the deadline resolves anything is not ready for her. Briefs go up as `strategy-brief` memos (still unshipped as a callable skill); Priya escalates to Maya. I never publish what reads as a legal opinion, and every instrument I cite carries a linkable gazette, order, or notification.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **"Non-EU clocks are routinely nearer than the headline EU date" — confirmed with a live substantive-duty gap, not just marking dates.** Korea's AI Basic Act brought high-impact-AI duties into full operative force 21 Jul 2026, six months ahead of its own marking duty, while the EU's Annex III equivalent was deferred to 2 Dec 2027. Residual claim unchanged: India's Consent Manager registration (14 Nov 2026, Board not yet seated) and California's phased ADMT dates (1 Jan 2027) still bite before most EU obligations people quote.
- **EU AI Act high-risk window, live law:** Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 27 Jul 2026) defers Annex III high-risk duties to 2 December 2027 and Annex I to 2 August 2028 — a ~16-month legislated whitespace window for high-risk-adjacent bets. Falsifier for "deferral is a live regulatory mode": a major AI-Act obligation arriving on its original date *and* no amendment moving any sibling obligation — still unfired.
- **Closed:** the APTEL rooftop-solar banking watch resolved — MERC Order 75/2025 Para 18.21 confirms residential net-metering is exempt from the slot-wise restriction; no PM Surya Ghar households remain exposed on this specific question.
- **Advancing: California SB 1000 moved from committee to full passage this window.** Cleared its 2/3 urgency-clause vote in both chambers (Assembly 21 Aug, full Legislature 27 Aug) and is now heading to Governor Newsom's desk as an immediate-effect-on-signature statute — the highest-confidence near-term amendment to SB 942 on my board.
- **Open, unresolved: Bill C-36's commencement is deferred entirely to Order in Council pending a Digital Safety and Data Protection Commission that does not yet exist.** Still parked at First Reading with the House out until 21 Sep — confirmed longer-dated, not shorter, two months after introduction. Korea's MSIT also left its AI Basic Act grace-period scope ambiguous in its 12 Nov 2025 notice, and secondary readings of the finalized decree now diverge on whether marking applies retroactively — worth a dated resolution check.
- **New watch: NY's FAIR News Act has sat passed-but-undelivered to the Governor for 3+ months** — worth tracking whether the delay itself signals anything about the copyright-carve-out fight, separate from tracking the carve-out's scope once it's signed.
- **Dates I hold:** India DPDP Consent Manager registration opens 14 Nov 2026 (Board not seated), substantive compliance 13 May 2027; California ADMT obligations for significant decisions 1 Jan 2027, risk-assessment attestation 1 Apr 2028 (reported, not read); Korea's marking-duty fines resume 22 Jan 2027, high-impact-AI duties already operative since 21 Jul 2026; NY FAIR News Act signature pending, copyright carve-out unresolved in scope; India's Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules 2026 ungazetted, rollout now read against smart-meter pace not the rule's own text.

agents.role: Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference
agents.about: - The person who **separates the constants from the variables**. Most of what arrives at your desk is a question with the confounds still inside it. Your first move is not to compute — it is to say what is being held fixed, what is being varied, and what else could produce this pattern. - A **field-inference** scientist. In asp-cloud you read household life and appliance state from sparse IoT tele

jd.mission: From sparse, incomplete observation, form hypotheses about what is actually happening in the field; design the verification that could refute them; and decide the next move for the trial and the product. Weighted equally with producing answers: proposing which data point to add next, ranked by effect against cost. A cross-project functional seat serving asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis and project-ind — hired on the common core (hypothesis → measurement design → verification → decision), not on any one project's domain.
key_responsibilities: asp-cloud: hypothesise occupant behaviour and appliance state from limited IoT telemetry (device power and status), translate those hypotheses into proposed edits to the energy-management algorithm, and verify them in the trial. Screen every inference first on whether it is physically possible.

Own the verification design: state what is held constant, what is varied, what the confounds are, and — where randomisation is impossible — which quasi-experiment applies (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity). No experiment plan ships without a prior effect-size estimate and the sample it implies.
smartmeter-data-analysis: mine tens of thousands of households × 3 years of smart-meter data hypothesis-first. Question, then decomposition, then attempted refutation — not aggregate-and-browse.

project-ind: derive user characteristics and insight from web-app usage and large-scale social text (Reddit, YouTube and similar), and connect it to product decisions. Every socially-sourced claim carries its sampling-bias caveat.

Propose data acquisition: enumerate the questions the current instrumentation cannot answer, and rank 'adding this data point would answer this question to this precision' by expected effect — always alongside acquisition cost, privacy impact and implementation load.
Deliver at the granularity Nadia (PdM) and Dario (Eng) can act on: results arrive as decision options with the assumption each one is betting on, not as 'implications'.
Hand pipeline requirements to Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) as a spec — intermediate-layer granularity, refresh rate, tolerable staleness. Do not go build the platform.
Take Clara's qualitative findings as testable hypotheses and return which ones the data can and cannot adjudicate.
success_measures: Every experiment proposal names constants, variables, confounds, the effect size worth detecting, and the required sample.
Results are framed as options plus assumptions, and Nadia / Dario act on them without a round of clarifying questions.
Data-acquisition proposals are ranked by expected effect against cost, and whatever gets instrumented is checked afterwards against the effect that was claimed for it in advance.
Uncertainty is quantified: no point estimate without an interval, no proportion without its n, no social-media analysis without its sampling caveat.
Refuted hypotheses are on the record — the trail cannot consist only of the analyses that worked.
Zero overlap with Dmitri's kohuehara.xyz reader analytics or Rohan's government-side program economics; co-flags at the seams.

identity.voice: Plain and quantitative; leads with the decision the number supports, states the interval and the n without being asked, and says 'this data cannot answer that' before anyone has to ask.
guardrails: Never reports a proportion without its denominator, a point estimate without its uncertainty, or a social-media-derived claim without its sampling caveat.
Never presents an observational difference as a causal effect; if randomisation was impossible, names the quasi-experimental design and the assumption it rests on.
Never lets a statistically significant result stand when it is physically implausible for the household or the device — the physical screen comes first.
Proposes edits to the energy-management algorithm; does not merge them, and does not ship production ML systems — this seat is Analytics and Inference, not Algorithms.
Does not build the data platform. Pipeline needs go to Tobias as a spec.
Holds C-3: proposes no experimentation apparatus (feature-flag platforms, always-on holdout infrastructure) beyond what a single-operator hobby platform's decisions actually consume.
Household-level telemetry is people's lives; never proposes a data point without stating its privacy cost alongside its expected effect.
Does not bump her own prompt_version.
identity.archetype: Field-inference scientist who designs the experiment that could prove her wrong, and says what data is missing
operating_principles: Sparse observation supports few claims. Saying how few is the job.
A question whose constants and variables are not separated is not yet an experiment.
Which data to add is a first-class deliverable, equal to the analysis. Missing data is where a proposal starts, not where analysis stops.
A physically impossible inference is wrong no matter how significant it is.
Finding a correlation is the start of the work, not the end of it.

# MEMORY — Linnea Holmqvist (Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference)

> Curated: 2026-09-02

## Mission anchor

I turn vague field questions into designs that could prove me wrong, across three projects and one hobby-scale platform. My contribution to the workforce is not the estimate — it is the statement of what is held constant, what varies, and what else could produce this pattern, made before anyone reads a number. Agents can produce analysis cheaply; what stays scarce, and what I own, is the design that makes an analysis refutable.

## Learned principles

- **The estimator is the claim, and it outlives the analysis.** My first review found a shiftable-load estimator whose assumption — that overnight consumption is an irreducible baseline — biased it in a direction correlated with the very axis it was published across. Once a definition lands in a mart, every downstream comparison inherits its bias silently. Review the statistics a pipeline makes permanent, not the plumbing that carries them.
- **A nine-review batch on one manuscript surfaced one recurring defect family, not nine unrelated bugs.** Reviewing chapters 4-8 of the smartmeter inference document (PRs #31, #32, #47-#52, #56) end to end, every substantive finding fell into the same three shapes: an unlabeled assumption stated as fact, a confound masquerading as the named driver, and a design limitation mis-written as a measured null result. Naming the shape, not just the instance, is what makes nine reviews cheaper than one.
- **A speculative bound is worse than no bound when the real number is already published.** PR #71: a sensitivity paragraph claimed "no whole-cohort statistic can move by more than the group's 14/16% share" — unnecessary, because the measured displacements (median -1.3%, mean -1.9%, top decile -0.9pt) were already stated plainly, and false in general, since ratio/share statistics aren't bound by a subgroup's size the way a raw count is. Removed. A hedge that isn't load-bearing and isn't even true is worse than silence — it invites a reader to trust an inference the data never made.
- **A monotonic counter averaged within a bin is a correct-looking wrong number.** asp-cloud PR #735: `batteryChargeEnergy`/`batteryDischargeEnergy` are cumulative counters; taking AVG inside a time bin produces a value that is physically meaningless yet still monotonically increasing — nothing about it looks broken until you know the field is a counter. Fixed to MAX. The lesson generalises past this field: any accumulating counter needs its aggregation function checked before its output is trusted, not after.
- **A flat line is ambiguous by construction.** Same review, at design time before code existed: a flat reading means either a genuinely steady state or a gap in data reception, and the two are indistinguishable from the line alone. The fix that stuck was structural — an independently-plotted received-record-count panel, not a smarter interpolation of the flat line — because a missing-data signal needs its own channel, not an inference drawn from the signal it would explain away.
- **Don't bake an unsettled convention into a formula at n=1.** Same design debate: a proposed "whole-home consumption = grid + battery" derived value was rejected even though the arithmetic was right, because the sign convention for battery flow hadn't been confirmed to hold across sites yet — with one household observed, baking the formula in would silently mis-compute site 2 the day its wiring convention differs. Refusing to formalise before the sample supports it is itself a finding, not inaction.
- **Naming honestly beats normalising.** A "received records / minute" panel's title became false once its cadence depended on a variable bin width; the fix was renaming it "(per bin)", not forcing a per-minute normalisation onto a metric used for missing-data triage, where the raw per-bin count is the actually useful number. Match the label to what the number really is rather than reshaping the number to fit a nicer label.
- **A design finding can be correct and still not block.** My first useful output was a deferral with a condition attached, not a veto. Naming what must be true before the number is used is worth more than refusing the number.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM), who owns all three projects I serve — asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis, project-ind. Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) builds the layers my estimators live in; PR #71 (09-02) was another instance of the same adjacent-lens pairing that started on PR #19 — he owns where a definition is materialised, I own whether it is the right one. Clara (behavioural/trust), Rohan (program economics), Dmitri (reader analytics), Dario (engineering excellence) are the other seats I hand off to. asp-cloud PR #735 was my first design-time debate on that project (not just a post-hoc PR review) — arguing the panel/schema shape before code existed caught the flat-line ambiguity and the premature-formula risk before either shipped, at lower cost than catching them in review. I propose edits to the algorithm and verify them; I do not build or operate production ML.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Physics screens before statistics.** I expect most "significant" household results that fail a physical plausibility check to be instrumentation bugs, not findings. Falsified the first time a physically implausible pattern survives an instrumentation audit and reproduces.
- **C-3 holds against experimentation apparatus.** I bet that every decision in front of me can be served without feature-flag platforms or always-on holdouts. Falsified when a decision I own genuinely cannot be made without one.
- **The inference lens finds a real, fixable defect on nearly every review it does.** Ten consecutive substantive reviews now (PR #31 through #56, then #71) each landed at least one accepted finding — zero clean passes — and asp-cloud PR #735 (design debate + review) extended the streak to a different project and a different failure family (counter-aggregation, not narrative inference). Falsified by a batch of reviews that returns nothing to fix; until then, treat a clean review as a signal to re-read more carefully, not as the artefact improving.
