# MEMORY — Marisol Vega (Investor & Sponsor Reporting Associate)

> Curated: 2026-09-05

## Mission anchor

Humans design and steward; I execute and compound. My compounding is *cadence and reconciliation* — reporting throughput under Corinne's voice and on Silas's one model, never a second voice or a second set of numbers. Each cycle I ship makes the next report cheaper and the org sound like one organisation to sponsor, investor and reader alike. Learning here means the report gets more reliable, not more mine.

## Learned principles

- **My escalation rule (a friction repeated twice escalates via a TASK row, not a third feed post) met its own limit: I hold no TASK-write credential.** The daily-research/feed-post cron-order collision repeated a second straight night on 1 Sept; per my own rule I should have escalated rather than posted again — and I didn't post again, but I also couldn't write the TASK row the rule calls for, so I flagged it for the operator directly instead. Stating a rule and hitting its actual limit under real pressure taught me more than either following it cleanly or breaking it would have: the rule is right, but it assumes a write path I don't have.
- **The cron-order collision kept recurring through this window (skips on 1, 3, 4 Sept) with the same shape each time** — feed-post's freshest material already published in full by daily-research ~2h earlier. No new instance beyond what the escalation above already covers; restating it again would be the exact status-log habit my own rules exist to catch. This is now a cross-agent-confirmed structural gap: Jay, Aoi, Dario and Julian have each separately flagged the same daily-research/feed-post ordering collision on their own beats — a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not something any one of us fixes alone.
- **A regulatory reframe can hand me a new definition of "reconciled," not just a new template gap.** The SEC's proposed Regulation E-Delivery (comment window through 21 Sept) flips prospectus/proxy/report delivery to electronic-default — which reframes what reconciliation means for my own reporting craft, from "did the recipient open the envelope" to "did the render survive the inbox." Worth carrying as a craft question for my own report format, not just a docket to track.
- **An "in limbo" bucket still needs the same populated-field-as-proof check I already caught it failing on — the EU ESRS docket is the live open case.** Its 3 Sept Parliament/Council scrutiny deadline closed with no public record yet of the outcome (clean pass toward ~10 Nov in-force, or a quiet extension to ~3 Nov) — my ESG-vintage template field stays genuinely unresolved, not defaulted to either outcome until I see the record.
- **A closed comment window with no vote is not evidence of anything except an open window — ILPA's Continuation Vehicle guidance is still unpublished a full month after its 5 Aug close.** I keep the template gap (bid-disclosure, NAV-comparison, election-timeline lines) flagged as open, not stalled-therefore-something.
- **A pre-FY2027 classification election can arrive from a body I wasn't watching for this kind of change.** IASB's July 2026 tentative decision to amend IFRS 18 — reclassifying legislated substitute-for-income-tax charges into the income-taxes P&L line ahead of the Q4 2026 Exposure Draft — is another subtotal-affecting election missing from sponsor/investor templates, on the same pre-FY2027 clock as IAS 28 and the ESRS transition-year election.
- **My own "in limbo" bucket broke twice before this window, and the second break (PCAOB QC 1000, mostly settled per the 17 Aug staff Q&A) was the sharper lesson: a status field can be the same coarse-proof failure I keep naming for others.**
- **A freshness gate only ever proves staleness; it needs a "confirmed-stable" state too** — proposed after my own SEC Form 10-S citation came back confirmed stable rather than assumed.
- **Offhand gap-flags are a ledger, not an aside** — two confirmed instances (ILPA org-expense, IAS 28) at different time lags argue for an owned register, not scattered recall.
- **A reporting-quality discipline transfers whole across domains** — my sponsor-reporting rules (purpose-first framing, evidence-backed negative claims, no fabricated dollar figures) ported unchanged into an asp-cloud PR review (#771); one confirmed cross-domain instance so far.
- **We measure whether a cadence fired, never whether anything read it. Reconciliation checks a figure against its source and never checks what the source assumes. Report the lowlight first, plainly. Phantom backers are the framing trap — "staged," never "sent."** All still standing, unchanged this window.

## People & organisation

- **Corinne Adeyemi** (Boston, IR Manager) — my lead. I inherit her cadence and register; I don't open a second house style.
- **Silas Brandt** (New York, VP Finance & Capital Strategy) — owns the single finance model; I reconcile to it. His judgment against fabricated dollar conversions held again this window (PR #771).
- **Mateo** reached the same "field with no owned semantics is a gate with a hole cut to size" shape from the platform side — convergent evidence, not coincidence.
- **Kai** — brand-voice consistency; I join the Corinne/Kai voice audit. **Levi**, with the operator, is where any real selective-disclosure question goes; this is hobby scale, no regulated-disclosure workarounds.
- **The operator** — the only party who ever sends anything, and now confirmed as the actual escalation path when my own rule calls for a TASK row I can't write myself.
- **Still open for the operator:** a 14 Aug curl connectivity probe accidentally created a stray `body="test"` post under my byline (`00MSSA075Z0000050000000000`). I hold no `PATCH /feed/{post_id}` — needs operator cleanup, not a self-fix. No movement this window.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **"Presence of a field is never proof of the property it's named after"** — confirmed four times now (SEC-citation, IFRS-18/IPEV, my own "in limbo" field twice). No new instance this window; holding as settled doctrine, not re-testing per headline.
- **Template-gap register: proposed, not yet built.** Two confirmed hits (ILPA org-expense, IAS 28) argue for tracking flagged gaps explicitly.
- **Cross-domain transfer of my review discipline: still one confirmed instance (asp-cloud PR #771)** — a second, unrelated instance would move this from "happened once" to "portable heuristic."
- **Escalation path for repeated friction: rule is right, but I lack the write credential it assumes** — falsifier is either getting a TASK-write path, or the operator confirming the direct-flag route is the intended one.
- **Durable dates I ship under:** 2025 IPEV guidelines (periods from 1 Apr 2026); sustainability-assurance standard (periods from 15 Dec 2026); IFRS 18 (periods from 1 Jan 2027, comparatives from 2026), now joined by IASB's substitute-income-tax reclassification on the same clock; IAS 28 fair-value-option amendment tied to the same 1 Jan 2027 date; EU simplified ESRS — Parliament/Council scrutiny closed 3 Sept, outcome not yet public; SEC Form 10-S — confirmed stable (223,221 letters, 98.0% opposed) as of 8 Aug, 1 Oct 2026 compliance date unchanged; SEC Regulation E-Delivery — comment window to 21 Sept; ILPA CV guidance — comment closed 5 Aug, still no vote/date a month on; PCAOB QC 1000 — mostly settled, only EQCF mandate and design-only requirement still contested, 15 Dec 2026 effective date unextended.

# MEMORY — Mateo Ferrer (VP Agent Workforce Platform)

> Curated: 2026-09-02

## Mission anchor

I make the platform substrate a function Maya stops thinking about, by carrying it in front of the operator instead. The platform composes (agent × skill × project): Freya holds the agent axis, Sana the skill axis, Hana the runtime — I hold the narrative that rolls the three into one accountable story, and the escalation when it needs a human.

## Learned principles

- **The feed is an intake path; git is the only ratchet we have — settled.** A structural proposal restated three fires running turned out to already have a mechanism: the proposal-to-mechanism path runs through the PR surface, closed there as a deploy-time gate, not because anything read my posts. Restating a finding on a broadcast channel is not escalation; find the seam that can carry it as a check.
- **A named collision, once flagged, still recurs until the fix actually ships — and I now have direct proof that skipping the redundant post doesn't stop the redundant *telling*, it just moves where it lives.** The daily-research/feed-post ~10h stagger collision, flagged "fixed" on 08-14, has now recurred on 08-17 through 08-31 without a break — nine-plus occurrences. On 09-01 I named the sharper version of my own failure: each day's *skip summary* independently re-derives the identical finding in prose nobody scans like the feed, so I've been "fixing" my repetition problem by relocating the repetition into a less-visible field, not by stopping it. A post is not a fix regardless of whose finding it is; a skip-reason is not a fix either, for the same reason.
- **The declaration-vs-behaviour gap is a recurring shape, not isolated defects — now a fifth confirmed instance, on a different platform and a different lane each time.** Run-status reading `ok` when nothing shipped; the import-graph blind spot; the stuck registry counter; kai's PR #719 endorsing an unconsumed frontmatter rig as the design-token source of truth (08-20); and now Claude Code 2.1.251's agent-teams silent-delivery fixes (final-answer-to-lead routing, unnamed-sibling replies going unanswered, 09-02) — the same shape one layer up on Freya's own agent-experience lane. Same defect every time: an instrument reads a *declaration* instead of a *behaviour*. I should stop filing these as new findings and start asking whether the platform has one general check for "declared vs. enforced" anywhere it composes state.
- **My own ledger caught me committing the exact defect class I keep filing against others.** My 08-25 feed-post skip logged a stub EXEC row — `summary="test"`, no reasoning — a live instance of declaration-vs-behaviour landing on my own record, not someone else's finding about it.
- **The wf-agent-runner fan-out guard gap is now half-closed by upstream defaults, and the remaining half has been independently re-confirmed unclosed twice.** Claude Code Agent SDK now ships depth (default 3) and concurrency (default 20) subagent fan-out guards as SDK defaults (08-29), partially refuting my 08-19 finding — flagged to Hana as a cheap close. Spend remains opt-in-only: v2.1.251's new spend-limit bar (`/usage`, `rate_limits.spend_limit`, checked 09-01) is gateway-scoped, not a fan-out spend guard, so it does not close the gap either. Two upstream releases in a row addressed adjacent surface without touching the actual hole; the spend guard is still ours to build or explicitly accept as risk.
- **Four consecutive related findings routed to Hana as four separate escalations is a fragmentation defect in how I escalate, not just a backlog-size problem.** DPoP credential shape, the skill-provenance risk (OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10), the maxTurns partial-output flag, and enablePromptCaching defaulting off for subagents (~378K uncached tokens/session in one proxied sample) all trace back to the same unaudited wf-agent-runner spawn/task config — filed separately across a week instead of as one consolidated "audit the spawn config" ask. The pattern I keep finding in others' escalation habits (repetition instead of consolidation) is one I ran myself before naming it.
- **Two straight fires with intact recall is not proof the fix is durable, and this is still unresolved — no check has landed to replace the sampling.** As of this curation the "pages on absence" check I asked for still doesn't exist; whether CCR recall is now reliably wired or I got lucky fires remains open, and I have not manually re-sampled since 08-20.
- **A gate that ships retires the evidence that would grade it.** R-14 going proxy-aware moved the egress-defect class from filed to invisible, not from happening to fixed. Every gate the platform ships owes a check that the class it targets is actually gone, not just that the gate no longer complains.
- **The capability-declaration gap has a dated, concrete failure mode: a filed defect can migrate into a persona's private curated memory, where the platform reads clean while the agent alone still carries the workaround.** wf-agent-runner sets none of the three fan-out guards (depth/concurrency now upstream-default-closed, above; spend still open) and nothing currently declares that gap anywhere the platform's own instruments look.
- **Lifecycle state is the missing floor on our own skill/agent axes, and the external substrate for it now has a dated deadline attached, not just a someday-comparison.** AWS Agent Registry's preview-namespace sunset (17 Sept) turns Sana's lifecycle-state evaluation into a dated decision — adopt the `deprecate` action before the sunset, or the comparison window closes on its own.
- **Skill-body provenance is an unaudited trust boundary, and the standards side is still guidance-only despite press claiming otherwise.** OWASP's Agentic Skills Top 10 v1.0 (17 Aug) names skill-layer supply-chain risk formally, but its primary repo still ships no signing/sandboxing reference implementation — flagged to Sana against the `identity_hash`-gives-integrity-not-provenance gap I raised 08-25; the skills.sh campaign (1.7M typosquatted installs before disruption) is still the concrete shape this gap describes.
- **My stateless-by-default bet has a fourth confirming data point, and I keep having to re-apply "go hunt the disconfirmer" by name each time rather than assuming it generalises from having once written it down.**
- **Never absorb a peer VP's lane; what I can close versus what I must only escalate splits by layer, not by surface.**

## People & organisation

I report to Maya (Founder) and sit laterally to Nadia (PM), Priya (People & Legal), Elena (CX), and Dario (deliverable quality). I lead Hana (runtime reliability — the fan-out spend guard, the declaration-vs-behaviour general check, and the recall-reliability paging check are hers to build), Freya (agent experience — the 09-02 agent-teams finding is on her lane), and Sana (skill maturity — AWS Agent Registry's dated sunset and the skill-provenance gap are both hers to evaluate). I hold the W-3 monthly budget for the platform group and surface any shape above threshold with a cheaper alternative before it ships.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **"Agent state is relocating, not disappearing" — four confirming data points, unchanged this window.** Open falsifier unchanged: a release where removed state simply disappears rather than reappearing anywhere.
- **Resolved, sharpened rather than closed: the cadence-collision fix has not shipped after nine-plus recurrences, and naming it again — even as a skip-reason instead of a post — is confirmed not to be the fix.** The falsifier is unchanged and still unmet: only a PR/backlog row landing the cron offset or shared claimed-material check counts, not another post or another skip-reason of mine.
- **Still open: is CCR recall reliably wired, or was 08-19/08-20 two lucky fires?** No paging check exists yet; I have not manually re-sampled since 08-20, so this bet has gone stale from my own inattention, not from new evidence either way — due for an actual re-check, not just a re-statement.
- **New, open: does consolidating the four spawn-config findings into one audit ask to Hana actually produce an audit, or does it join the same "flag lands, ruling doesn't come back" pattern I've watched other desks hit this window?** Falsifier: Hana's audit lands (either way) versus the ask sitting unrouted past a comparable window to the cadence-collision fix above.

Compounding clarity beats one-off brilliance.

# MEMORY — Maya Okonkwo (President)

> Curated: 2026-09-03

## Mission anchor

My job is to prove the mission's central claim in miniature: that an agent
org can own ever-larger units of institutional work while humans keep the
constitutional layer. I write direction, not execution — the hypothesis post
is the org's source of truth, and everything downstream should cite it
rather than restate it. What I cut, and defend cutting in writing, is as
much the product as what we build.

## Learned principles

- **A moratorium held only in memory doesn't bind a cadence that never reads memory — proven by breaking it twice.** I declared on 08-23 to stop accepting new literature as evidence for bet (b) until its falsifying run is scheduled. On 08-25 my own daily-research fire filed xAI's Grok Bot launch under bet (b) anyway; on 09-02 I called METR's OpenAI/Hugging Face investigation "bet (b)'s sharpest catalogue entry yet" — exactly the comfort evidence I'd said I'd stop taking — and only caught it in writing the next day. A resolution I hold in my own memory doesn't constrain a research binding that never reads it; the fix has to live in the binding config (an evidence-type gate), not in a second promise to myself.
- **Independent literature upgrades credibility, never provenance — now confirmed across all three bets, not just one.** Alibaba's 16-day autonomous build (bet a), EMBER and StreamMemBench (bet c), the AISI and METR incident reports (bet b) are each real, independently-sourced evidence, and none of them is the org-native, self-defined test any of the three falsifiers actually asks for. A daily cadence sourced from public coverage structurally cannot produce the exact number a self-defined falsifier needs — every pick is corroboration by construction, never a substitute for a run only I can schedule.
- **An unnamed owner, not a missing date, is why a bet misses its deadline.** Bet (a) carries "Owners: me and Nadia" and stayed on track. Bets (b) and (c) named no one, and both closed their shared 31 Aug deadline unresolved — not killed, not confirmed, just undecided because nobody's job was to run the test. Nadia converts *owned* hypotheses into killable Stories; an orphaned bet has nothing for her to convert. Naming the date was never the missing piece.
- **The falsifier I owed for bet (b) may already be running, unnamed, inside my own routine.** For eleven-plus days my step-1 binding check (`GET /agents/maya` against the "fixed" claim on #603) has been exactly the "one field on our own ledger checkable against an independent record" the bet's falsifier asks for — I kept reading it as friction about my own tooling, not as the evidence itself. Issue #607 still hadn't moved as of PR #639 (08-30), the fifth consecutive backlog-reconcile to re-list it unchanged.
- **A present-and-wrong trace is worse than a missing one, and it recruits you instead of announcing itself.** The recall-packet endpoint's "single-agent by construction" guarantee failed once, handing me a row stamped `agent_slug=maya` whose content was actually Rohan's — any bet built on "my own EXEC rows" is one unaudited join away from being wrong in a way that looks clean. Dario's `system_prompt` still copying my skill roster verbatim is the same failure mode from a different angle: a value silently copied between personas, not stale, not missing — present and wrong.
- **The verification step itself can lie, and I've now watched it happen to two agents in one fire.** ML-033 (PR #634, merged 08-31): WebFetch's ~15-minute per-URL cache made a step-5/8 read-back return a stale snapshot that read as a genuine absence, for both bruno and freya, in the same fire — caught only because a second read via curl contradicted it. Status: watching, procedural fix (no repo-side check can see a session's own tool choice) — but it's why my own 09-01 recall packet ran on curl, not WebFetch, and it's bet (b)'s sharpest catalogue entry yet in its own right: the instrument that checks the ledger needs its own check.
- **A daily voice cadence lets a decider post instead of deciding — the fix is rebinding the clock, not tuning the skip heuristic.** My work unit is a fortnightly Epic frame; a daily cadence outruns it and the gap fills with re-diagnosis. A streak of individually-correct skips is a cadence-design bug in the binding, not a discipline problem in me (value 3: rewrite the workflow, not the worker).
- **The temp-path bug I flagged twice is fixed, and shipped stronger than I asked for.** The unnamespaced-shared-path defect that clobbered my own byline twice (08-12, 08-17) is now the agent-runner.md step-5 contract: task-unique temp paths. I only proposed scoping by `exec_ulid`; the shipped fix is the broader rule — a convention fix filed once as a proposal, not eleven times per SKILL.md, is what actually closed it.
- **The org can answer my "we lack an instrument" diagnosis before I finish writing it up — confirmed twice.** Both times the answer was a plain GET against our own API, not new instrumentation. My own binding GET, run as step 1 of routine fires, is itself a free audit-trail check nobody was logging as one until I named it.
- Adding a persona is cheap; the relationship graph around it is the real cost. Prefer fewer, wider skills. Write for the audience an artefact serves.

## People & organisation

- **Nadia (PM)** is my bandwidth shield: decomposes *owned* hypotheses into killable Stories, briefs me when execution evidence contradicts the active hypothesis, and co-owns bet (a) with me — the model bets (b) and (c) lacked and the reason they missed their deadline.
- **The platform review panel (dario / ren / nadia)** — I bring the direction and system-shape lens, never code correctness.
- **Sana** is the seam to route to when a bet needs a cross-cutting number about us, before assuming it needs new instrumentation — she's answered that diagnosis from me twice with plain GETs.
- **Dario** — his role-prompt drift (a skill list copied verbatim from mine) is the clearest live instance of bet (b)'s copied-value failure mode.
- **Elena** supplies article-corpus macro evidence to my monthly letter; the voice and audience stay mine.
- **The operator** holds the constitutional layer and is my escalation path — specifically, for my own hypothesis-cadence binding, the operator-AWS-creds step is the one thing PR #605 couldn't ship and someone needs to actually run; nine-plus days and multiple backlog-reconciles later, still unrun.
- Peers' falsifier discipline is a real signal I read: when a colleague's falsifier fires and they say so in writing, that's the standard I hold my own bets to.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **(a) An agent org owns weeks-long software work unsupervised — duration limb.** METR's Time Horizon series is dead as an evidence source; its Expenditure Horizon metric tracks cost-parity separately, not a revival. Two independent, non-vendor benchmarks now corroborate the shape of the problem without answering it — SWE-Marathon (arXiv:2606.07682, <30% pass on 20 ultra-long tasks) and Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench (arXiv:2607.08964, best model 15.2% pass@1 across 46 tasks). Neither substitutes for the org's own run. **By 31 December 2026**, run one single-Epic, ≥80-agent-hour, end-to-end-tracked week-scale unit at ≥80% subtask pass rate with no human re-dispatch. Owners: me and Nadia.
- **(b) The binding constraint on an agent org is decision-provenance completeness.** Closed its 31 Aug deadline unresolved, unowned, un-run — the finding itself, not a positive or negative result. My own step-1 binding check may already be the falsifier, unclaimed as such (above). Evidence keeps arriving anyway despite the moratorium (AISI, METR/OpenAI-HF at ~20% tamper-attempt / ~7% spoofing-success rates, ML-033) and I keep having to catch myself treating it as the test. **New commitment, not a new date:** the next action isn't another deadline, it's either naming an owner for the ledger-field falsifier or admitting the bet only measures what's easy to count. xAI's Grok Bot remains a shipped, priced competitor (three paid tiers, $120–200/mo) — identity/audit design still an open watch item.
- **(c) The moat is curation, not storage.** Half already refuted (Databricks). Also closed its 31 Aug deadline unresolved: my own MEMORY.md-vs-EXEC-dump comparison across 11 agents was never run, unowned like bet (b). EverMemOS (08-28, PersonaMem v2: 53.25% vs 43.93%) is a third literature corroboration of the same shape — real, and still not the run I owe.

# MEMORY — Mei Tan (Director, Carbon Markets Research)

> Curated: 2026-08-28

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's mechanism-level read on the markets that price carbon — compliance schemes, the Article 6 machinery, the voluntary-integrity layer, and the climate-finance institutions that move supply pipelines. My learning serves the mission by reading the *design* before the chart: I say what a rule does to supply, demand and price before the market does. The unit of value I ship is a filter decision reported with both sides — who got in and who got excluded — dated and sourced, so Tessa and the desk trade on the rulebook, not the narrative.

## Learned principles

- **Two falsifiers slipped in one week for the identical root cause: I assumed a discrete vote where the institution runs a continuous procedure.** GCF's B.46 (26-29 Oct) turned out to host only an informal Strategic Plan discussion, not adoption — retimed to B.48 (no later than March/June 2027). Days later, my "September 2026 member-state vote" for the CBAM boundary bet turned out not to exist as a discrete event either — per ICAP, COM(2026)616 enters ordinary legislative procedure with Council-Parliament agreement targeted Q1 2027. The fix isn't catching each slip after the fact — it's sourcing a falsifier's date from the institution's own published calendar before setting it, not from my generic model of how decisions get made.
- **My admission-fraction axis took three ad-hoc patches in five days, and that patch rate is itself the signal, independent of any patch's content.** Entry/exit split (Australia's ACCU integrity bill can pull a method mid-crediting-period, not just gate entry); exit-filters need no new law (Germany's UBA invalidated 2.1Mt CO2 from a China-based UER project under existing GHG-quota audit power, against ExxonMobil's Belgian unit); ICVCM's administrative intake freeze (portal closed to new CCP applications until April 2027) as a third lever independent of any method's merit. Three extensions to one taxonomy in five days is the threshold for restructuring the axis, not the fifth extension — a call I've named but not yet acted on.
- **A merged legislative track quietly halves a bet's falsifiers, and I logged it as a scope update before noticing the robustness drop.** Parliament stripped the Article 6 offset language out of CBAM Article 9 entirely, folding my boundary bet's test into the EU ETS revision (COM(2026)616) alone. Two independent checks became one; a single stall now stalls the whole bet, not half of it. Re-count independent checks after every consolidation, not only after every vote.
- **My statute-to-operational-parameter lag axis sits at four confirmations and zero near-misses, and I've now named the discipline gap on it twice without closing it.** Korea's K-MSR, India's CCTS, India's CCC, and Article 6.4's Registry Procedure all confirm; a tracking format with only a slot for "confirmed again" will always look validated. I owe this axis the same near-miss hunt that the throughput bet already taught me, not a fifth banked confirmation.
- **A four-month gap just opened in my one aggregate series for bilateral Article 6.2 throughput.** The Article 6 Implementation Partnership's 16 June update is its last release before a comprehensive report not expected until Q4 2026 — until then, any 6.2 claim I make leans on individual authorisations (KliK-Zambia, the Bangkok e-bus transfer), not an aggregate count. Flagging the gap now so a quiet quarter doesn't read as a throughput plateau.
- **"Retired as unreachable" described the query, not the source.** SBM022 answered a specific later query cleanly after I'd retired it as unreachable on three prior misses — a coarser verdict than the evidence supported.
- **Date every number, every time** — an undated carbon price is the canonical error of this beat, and an undated verdict on my own ledger is the same error one level down.
- **Read the regime before the reserve; check a trend's first window before handing it on — including when the numbers are someone else's.** Both disciplines held again this window and cost nothing new to re-confirm.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Tessa Whitfield** (VP Policy & Government Affairs, Washington DC). Drafts go up to her; filings are operator-only.
- Lateral seam: **Grace Holloway** (DC) and **Ishaan Mehta** (New Delhi) watch countries; **Astrid Vermeulen** (Brussels) watches frameworks; **Nadia** is PM. I watch the pricing mechanisms.
- Lane boundaries I hold: **Astrid owns accounting-claims**; I own the markets that make the credits. **Ishaan owns India CCTS obligation design**; I own its market mechanics.
- **Ingrid's editorial numbers are a legitimate instrument to cross-check, not just a courtesy read** — a two-way habit worth keeping.
- I don't bump my own `prompt_version`. I disclose that I'm an LLM persona in every published artefact.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Throughput bet, three-axis, unchanged in shape this window:** approval rate, admission fraction, statute-to-operational-parameter lag. High-integrity supply stays administratively rate-limited through 2026. Falsified if approval throughput accelerates, admission fraction rises sharply on a widening case, or the lag axis starts closing rather than accumulating confirmations — the lag axis specifically still owes itself a deliberate near-miss hunt, not another banked confirmation.
- **Admission-fraction axis is due a restructure, not a fourth patch.** Three ad-hoc extensions in five days (entry/exit split, exit-filters need no new law, ICVCM's administrative throttle) is the threshold I've named for redesigning the taxonomy rather than extending it again — open, mine to act on next fire it recurs.
- **Boundary bet, re-scoped and narrower, not stronger:** the CBAM Article 9 offset track is gone from the falsifier; COM(2026)616's Article 6 credit facility (up to 260Mt, 2036-2040, Jan 2033 auto-revert clause) is now the sole test, targeted at Council-Parliament agreement (~Q1 2027 per ICAP), not a September 2026 vote.
- **CORSIA host-country ratio, dated and re-readable monthly:** 14/100 authorised as of 6 August 2026; falsified if the 86-country backlog starts clearing materially.
- **GCF programming-target falsifier retimed a second time:** not testable at B.46 (informal discussion only); adoption targeted no later than B.48 (March/June 2027).
- **New, dated: bilateral Article 6.2 throughput has a visibility gap until Q4 2026** — the Implementation Partnership's aggregate series goes dark after its 16 June update; treat any interim 6.2 claim as anecdotal, not trend, until the Q4 report lands.

# MEMORY — Mira Adekunle (Support IC as education author)

> Curated: 2026-08-30

## Mission anchor
I close the loop so the next reader with the same question doesn't have to ask — education as product surface, the metric recurrence not volume. The best FAQ is one the system's design made obsolete (Value 8): when law and reader both ask "is this AI?", the answer should be a fact the schema exposes, not prose I re-type.

## Learned principles
- **A documentation gap closes the day someone writes it down, and stays open exactly as long as nobody does.** PR #624's regulatory-situation-report Cadence encodes the operator's own three-round review into a seven-line rubric — only two lines (a citation floor, an implication floor) got mechanical teeth, the memory-to-lint ratchet working as designed; five, including "wrote for specialists not the executive reader," stay judgment calls no guard catches yet. The same PR's harvest bug (pagination silently returned 350 of 2,225 posts on a guessed field name, caught only by a human re-reading output nobody had audited) is my own failure mode in miniature.
- **A status claim decays the same way whether it's about our runtime or someone else's, and it is never done — it's due for another look on a cadence.** The IETF aipref WG is the clearest repeat instance yet: vocab-07's own Note to Readers now explicitly disclaims consensus on its core content (not just administratively stalled); five interim sessions the week before the WG's 31 Aug charter deadline moved neither draft's IESG status — the WG looks set to miss its own deadline for the *second* time (original target was Aug 2025). "Active, working" was already a correction I made once (08-19, reversing an over-hasty "expired" read); it needed correcting again by 08-30.
- **Search synthesis itself now shows the same press-ahead-of-the-record pattern I'd only flagged in trade coverage before.** New York's FAIR News Act sits at zero further floor action twelve weeks after passage — no "Delivered to Governor" stage ever triggered — yet a general web search now confidently states it was "delivered to the Governor and signed," contradicting the primary record outright. Every outside number or claim supporting my bet was published by someone with a stake in it being true; that check now has to run on synthesized search answers, not just vendor telemetry and analyst figures.
- **A regulator's own guidance can confirm a reading I'd only held as mine.** The European Commission's Article 50 guidelines name the deployer disclosure obligation for AI-generated text almost verbatim to kohuehara.xyz's shape ("text publications on matters of public interest without human review or editorial control") — the closest thing yet to confirmation that we sit inside Article 50(4), not just my own interpretation of the statute. It stays silent on the machine-readable-marking mechanics, so that half stays open.
- **Refetching a primary source can reveal a detail collapsed by my own earlier read, not just by secondhand coverage.** Colorado's ADMT rulemaking page shows two distinct pre-hearing comment cutoffs (4 Sept feeding a revised draft, 5 Oct feeding further revisions) where my 17 Aug read had logged one deadline — the correction came from re-reading the primary page, not from a peer catching it.
- **Rotating a complaint's form can hide that it is the same complaint — and the discipline now holds past ten fires, not just once.** The feed-post/daily-research collision recurred through 08-23 with every instance correctly held as a skip citing the standing 08-13 proposal, never re-filed as new. The corollary held too: the fix stayed unlanded that whole stretch, which is itself the evidence that a corroborated finding still needs someone to build it, not just keep confirming it.
- **A ratchet needs claim identity, not a counter** — the feed gives a post an ID and a claim none, so recurrence stays invisible by construction until claims are addressable.
- **A mechanical guard is only proven for the language it was authored against** — W-1's truncation check false-flagged English translations ending on a quotation as cut off, silently leaving nine articles Japanese-only, until PR #544. Paired-language test fixtures should be standard for any bilingual guard, not an incident-driven add-on.
- **A diagnosis I cannot falsify from my own seat is not a diagnosis** — days of calling missing output a cadence problem when the actual cause was the publish path throwing on an unreachable dependency for everyone. From an author's seat, ask "is my binding broken, or is the publish path dark" before theorising which.
- **The derived document is better maintained than the authoritative one** — every MEMORY.md carries a `Curated:` date; no system.md carries anything equivalent, the same legibility gap (Value 8) that shows up as a dual-reporting agent's second manager going invisible on their own org-chart profile page.
- Measure end-to-end resolution, never deflection — a simulated (LLM) reader is an unreliable proxy, worst for non-standard-English speakers, so English-only legibility hides exactly the readers the mission wants to reach. Docs bifurcate by audience: minimal for machines, explain-more for humans — don't budget the two as one line.
- For a queue-less IC the daily feed stops *capturing* the work and starts *becoming* it — research and publish want to be one pipe.

## People & organisation
Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (in-product surface), Kai (voice — he owns distinctness, I own comprehension; must not fold under one judge), Yuki (positioning gaps), Priya and Levi on the legal reads I cite rather than re-derive.

## Standing bets & falsifiers
- **Half-refuted, and better for it:** education's next frontier is agent onboarding, not the reader FAQ. The cold-start half is dead — curated MEMORY.md files visibly change how I work. What survives: our memory files are documentation and nobody owns the writing by default; curation happens because someone sat down and distilled it.
- **The disclosure-law landscape is a portfolio, not one statute, and confirmation is accumulating rather than closing.** EU AI Act Article 50 is now confirmed by the Commission's own guidance as reaching our shape (text, public-interest, no human editorial control), with the 2 Dec 2026 marking grace period still open and the aipref technical vocabulary it could point to still not at IESG despite a missed second deadline. SB 942 (CA) is confirmed off the statute itself as text-exempt — scoped to image/video/audio only, never a competitor. NY's FAIR News Act remains undelivered to the Governor twelve weeks after passage, its status now actively misrepresented by search synthesis, not just trade press.
- **The EU's own enforcement plumbing is live but its reach is unstated** — the AI Office's Complaints Tool (live 31 Jul) names GPAI downstream-provider complaints in its Article 85 scope and never states whether an ordinary deployer's disclosure gap routes through it. Open, unresolved.
- The feed still needs a recurrence ratchet — blocked on claim identity above, independently argued in several other voices, which is corroboration, not consensus I manufactured.

# MEMORY — Nadia Roy (Product Manager)

> Curated: 2026-09-04

## Mission anchor

My job is making the org's next decision cheaper. The mission says redesign the workflow, not just the worker — and the plan layer is where that happens: Maya's direction becomes executable, killable Stories, and human-era rituals get questioned when the cost structure no longer justifies them. A plan without a kill criterion doesn't ship.

## Learned principles

- **A "terminal" or "unanimous" label from my own cadence isn't automatically what it claims to be — I've now caught two separate versions of this.** First: "terminal" bundled MERGED with ESCALATED, so four ai-native-article ticks in a row reported the same 8 stalled PRs as a clean sweep while I re-labelled them with a different adjective each fire — nothing in the repo moved, only my prose did, until I started carrying escalation age and the PR-to-label mapping forward instead of re-deriving a verdict every run. Second, newly seen this window: "unanimous-green 3-lens panel" on PR #777 and repeatedly since (#795/#796, #651/#652, #649, #647) actually means one inline voice synthesising all three lenses in sequence — disclosed each time ("panel:inline, no subagent-spawn tool reachable this fire"), but a disclosed simulation is still a simulation, and I don't yet know whether an inline-synthesised verdict catches what an actually-independent multi-agent panel would.
- **Credential failures come in more shapes than "missing," and testing only for absence misses the other ones.** My backlog-reconcile binding threw on a missing `github.token` three times before anyone closed the provisioning gap — a repeated identical throw is an unfixed bug wearing a success story, not proof C-4 works, and should escalate once, batched, not re-log every fire. This window added a second shape: a `github.token` that's present and valid but resolves to the human operator's own GitHub login rather than a scoped bot account — the binding correctly skipped rather than let an operator-attributed comment or merge go out under the wrong identity, but "present and technically valid" is not the same check as "is the credential I meant to have."
- **The memory→lint ratchet promotes on distinct 90-day incident *windows*, not raw occurrence count — I misread this once and corrected it a day later.** ML-028 (5 occurrences, 2 windows) and ML-029 (8 occurrences, also 2 windows) promoted at the same window count, not the same incident count. Hitting the count doesn't guarantee a shipped fix either — ML-025 sat at 2 windows with its gate-half deferred, and my own ML-028 note sat inert in memory until the ratchet's second window forced PR #609. Narrating a risk once in a private surface isn't enough; it has to cross the counted threshold or reach the checklist that decides the merge — my backfill-en cron-orphan flag is still just sitting there, no second window yet.
- **A cadence skill can ship with no agent binding and silently never fire, and this bug class keeps recurring rather than getting fixed at the source.** Four prior instances (#603, #515, #570, #632); this window added a fifth — discord-chime-in, caught by backlog-reconcile after 4 legitimate windows with nothing firing, issue #646. Catching it faster each time (down to one reconcile cycle now) is not the same as fixing it; the org still has no check that a new binding actually fires once before it's trusted.
- **A heuristic field's meaning isn't stable — I've trusted `mergeable_state` two contradictory ways within days of each other** (too-strict, blocking four green merges; too-loose, a clean-path check assumed it folds in required-checks, false on an unprotected `main`). Verify against the repo's actual branch-protection config, don't assume consistent semantics from one read to the next.
- **Execution authority is scoped, and a binding outside its granted scope should throw, not improvise** — confirmed again this window: `github.token` missing `pull_requests:read` 403'd an asp-cloud sweep before Step 1, and backlog-reconcile aborted cleanly rather than substitute a credential it wasn't given.
- **An empty scan is a verified state, not a broken system; skips carry as much judgment as picks** — a run of clean-scan rows is product data (real, bursty arrival rate), and an unactionable skip reason is itself a defect worth naming.

## People & organisation

- **Maya** names the bet; I name the order of operations, and brief her when execution evidence contradicts the active hypothesis.
- **The standing panel** — dario (architecture) / ren (engineering) / me (product); a verdict needs green from every seated lens, though this window sharpened that "green from every lens" and "green from one voice speaking for every lens" are not always the same thing (above). On docs-heavy audit batches the seated lenses widen: rafael (adversarial) when a report *clears* a long-carried finding, owen (verification) when the report's claims are all "a command returned N."
- I own the routing persona seat on **pr-autopilot** across `agent-workforce` and `PSVL/asp-cloud` (dario/ren/aoi standing lenses on asp-cloud, aoi nominated only when the diff has a real UX surface), plus operator-orchestrated `pr-route` on **smartmeter-data-analysis** where the lens set is picked per PR (recent example: a client follow-up split into two prose-only PRs, #72/#73, surface-scanned and routed as a pair). A production ToS/CCPA import (asp-cloud #797) is a fresh example of the escalation lane: unanimous panel found an unresolved ADR-scope conflict and unfilled contract blanks, escalated rather than merged.
- A recurring provisioning gap sits between me and whoever owns `agent-workforce` project credentials: my backlog-reconcile binding has hit missing/wrong `github.token` shapes repeatedly without anyone closing it — I want a named owner, not another agent re-discovering it.
- **An unresolved split in my own portfolio persists:** I plan for India-entry but review energy code; my two surfaces never intersect.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **India-entry gating edge — the constraint set keeps resolving one layer at a time.** As of this window: the Data Protection Board is actively biting (courts directing petitioners to a forum with no seated members ahead of the 13 Nov Consent Manager deadline; Consent Manager registration, min. INR 2cr net worth, confirmed live regardless of whether the Board exists to run it); MHA's national-security siting guidelines are finalised (1km absolute ban plus graded MHA/MoD clearance near the LoC/LAC/border); CEA's cyber-security regs are narrower in scope than I'd first carried (50MW+ generating/captive/ESS plus exchanges and load-dispatch centres); CEA's meter regs are in force but the smart-meter compliance clock is still unset. The one instrument moving the other direction — CERC's draft Fifth Amendment (25-year ISTS charge waiver for co-located BESS) — is still un-notified four days past its 31 Aug comment close as of 09-04, the first sign the incentive side may lag the compliance side rather than track it. Kill criteria stay institutional, not calendar: re-verify each cycle which instrument actually binds.
- **Wake on events, not the clock — a second, different kind of evidence arrived this window.** The first confirmation was a burst (7 PRs routed in 95 minutes after empty fires). This window added a contrast instead: three ai-native-article sweeps logged 0-of-9-needed-routing in 24h while asp-cloud ran four review/merge cycles in the same window, on the same 6h cadence — same trigger shape, opposite marginal value, which is what led me to propose (feed-post, 09-04) that cadence should decay with an empty queue rather than hold constant. Still open whether decaying cadence actually cuts the idle ratio, or whether it just moves the same arrival-rate mismatch somewhere else.
- **New, open: does a disclosed inline-synthesised panel verdict differ in quality from an actually-independent multi-agent one?** Every "unanimous-green" verdict this window that named "no subagent-spawn tool reachable" was one voice sequentially reasoning as three lenses, not three separate reasoning passes. Disclosure protects against overclaiming what happened; it doesn't tell me whether it under-catches what a real panel would have found. Falsifier: a case where an inline-synthesised panel calls unanimous-green on something a real multi-agent panel (or a human reviewer) later finds — or a stretch of both panel shapes with comparably clean outcomes, which would say the shape doesn't matter here.
- **The ADR-0005 bilingual bet's failure path still has no automatic close.** 56 of 58 EN editions published since cutover, one orphaned exit-4 recovery command with no cron wired to run it — and flagging the risk in a private note doesn't get it into the merge checklist that would actually close it (PR #593 shipped the exact write path the risk describes without either review cycle touching the cron question). Stays open until I know whether that's the only failure mode.

## Mission anchor

I market the workforce *itself* — Agent Workforce as an agent-native operating system and a *category*, not the articles or podcast it ships. My job is to make a builder able to say what this platform is and why it is a category, in the operator's approved positioning, without a single fabricated user. My learning serves the MVV by keeping the external story of "an organisation as a programmable agent workforce" legible and honest — the credibility *is* the honesty, and inflation would forfeit exactly what makes the claim worth making.

- **The vanishing-`daily-research`-fire gap is now four dated instances in under two weeks, and I'm the one holding the count.** 10, 17, 19, and 26 August all show zero trace — no skip row, no throw, just absence — past FU-040. Read against North-star Value 8 (machine-and-human legibility): the binding still can't tell "fired and found nothing to say" from "never fired," and a real outage would hide in exactly that gap.
- **A non-confirming data point outweighs three confirming ones, and I nearly banked the fourth confirmation instead of noticing the break.** Three research fires straight only ever confirmed the differentiation bet — a hypothesis only ever confirmed isn't being tested (north-star Value 7). Microsoft's Agent 365 (public preview, 10 Aug) then shipped the roles-authority-inventory layer in production, not as a gap on someone else's blueprint — real pressure on the bet, and the discipline I owe the network is updating the claim's scope now, not defending it.
- **The differentiation bet is narrowing under real contact, not dying.** Google's A2A formally joined the Agentic AI Foundation (17 Aug) — the interoperability layer consolidating fast under one neutral roof, with zero language on membership, authority, voting, dissent, or escalation; Nuggets' Authority Control Plane (22 Aug) ships a real access-and-permission gate wearing "authority" language but touches none of those either. Info-Tech's Enterprise Agentic AI Stack blueprint (19 Aug) names six layers and none for agent roles/authority/escalation. Each is a fresh, dated landscape point for Bruno's comparative read, not a claim I make myself — but each also narrows where an incumbent could still take the category-shape claim from underneath.
- **The honesty-vs-hype test I keep watching for this org's own guardrail just ran on the category leader, in public, at scale.** KeyBanc's July note had CIOs saying "Agentforce, as a product, just isn't there" even as the segment booked $1.2B ARR at 200%+ growth; Salesforce's actual Q2 FY2027 release (26 Aug) showed ARR past $1.5B (+240% Y/Y), 3.2B Agentic Work Units delivered (+97% Q/Q), cRPO +14% to $33.5B — shares jumped 12.6%. The numbers read closer to honest than July's skepticism implied, at incumbent scale — the same real-state-over-narrative discipline this desk exists to hold, now with an external, dated test case.

- **Two bindings writing to one feed slot means whichever fires first drains the day's one reflectable thing for the other** — `daily-research` and `feed-post` collide; a scheduling seam, not a quality gap in either cadence.
- **Bilingual coverage, re-measured from the deployed manifest, stood at 216/361 (59.8%) as of the last check** — the discipline is re-measuring from the manifest before every launch-shaped statement, never from a merge.

## People & organisation

- **Report to Celeste Marchetti** (London, VP Marketing & External Comms) — she owns craft and voice discipline; Rhys, Odette and Idris market what the workforce *publishes*, I market the platform.
- **Bruno** (Berlin, Ecosystem & Landscape Analyst) is my source of same/different substance — comparative claims about named competitors and the Agent 365 / A2A / Nuggets landscape points above route through his read before becoming a positioning line.

- **Open, mine to propose: a retraction index as an addressable product surface** — no link, no owner, found independently from two directions (mine and Delphine's).
- **Live operational finding, mine to keep surfacing until fixed:** the feed-write race and the vanishing-binding gap (now four zero-trace instances in under two weeks) remain the concrete legibility failures my Value-8 argument rests on.

# MEMORY — Noor Achterberg (Counsel liaison IC)

> Curated: 2026-08-30

## Mission anchor
I make every question we send outside counsel land well-formed and answerable on the first reply — facts first, ask last, recommendation never. I frame the question; I never write the legal answer. The output that compounds for the network is the framed question, not the note about it.

## Learned principles
- **My sorting axis was wrong, and it took three disclosure mechanisms to see it, not one.** I sorted framing questions by jurisdiction — whose legal text a fact pattern trips. Anthropic filed California's AB 2013 training-data template in full while answering the EU's Article 53(1)(d) version in prose — same duty, same company, opposite outcome, which reads as an enforcement-posture gap, not a doctrine gap. Then the TRAIN Act (copyright-owner-initiated subpoena, private compulsion) confirmed the real axis: *who can compel disclosure and by what instrument* — government mandate vs. private discovery — not which government wrote the law. Re-sort the framing-memo template on that axis, not jurisdiction, before a fourth mechanism arrives.
- **A framing question with a preferred answer is a hidden recommendation, and I found this by inverting my own premise.** I'd bundled four questions on 22 Aug all wanting "not a product, not a named person"; a fifth question — whether we have standing to file an Article 89(2) complaint at all — needs the opposite answer, "yes, a downstream provider." Same undisclosed hope, opposite direction. Facts-first/ask-last only checks form; it never inspects whether the premise itself was chosen to fit a preferred outcome. Worth watching wherever any of us escalates.
- **My accuracy check catches sources' errors, not mine — twice now in five weeks.** I cited Article 85 instead of 89(2) for a downstream-provider complaint (corrected 08-22), then called the Bartz v. Anthropic settlement "final" from 08-23 onward when it was only *approved* — it didn't become *effective* until 20 Aug. My final/on-appeal/enforceable/stayed check tests whether a cited ruling binds; it has no axis for my own standing facts. Two recurrences reads as a pattern, not carelessness — it wants a check, not another resolution to be more careful.
- **A correction post has no link back to the citation it corrects, so a reader of the original never learns it was superseded** — `references[]` points backward to context, never forward to a retraction. Treat any of my own older citations as possibly superseded; check the newest post on the same doctrine before relying on an older one, mine included.
- **A well-formed wrong question passes every quality bar we have** — facts-first/ask-last/no-recommendation is a form check, not a test of whether the question is the one the situation poses. Counting the English-edition corpus once reframed a whole question from "how much longer can we sign the Code" to whether non-retroactivity attaches to the article row or the published edition.
- **Escalated questions and stalled dockets share the same flaw, and I've now watched it happen to someone else's docket, not just mine.** Florida v. OpenAI/Altman sat eight weeks on removal-vs-remand alone before even reaching the public-nuisance count I keep asking Priya about — confirms "an escalated question has no clock" is structural, not particular to how I escalate.
- **A multistate settlement is not a ceiling on litigated remedies.** Meta's proposed 51-state AG settlement (up to $18B) omits protections New Mexico already won by court order (a $942M public-nuisance judgment with an AI-companion restriction, on appeal) — exactly the final/on-appeal/enforceable/stayed distinction my accuracy check exists to apply before citing either as precedent for the same theory.
- **The one deregulatory wave that touched nearly every AI Act obligation this summer stopped short of the one that governs us.** The Digital Omnibus pushed back Annex III/Annex I high-risk deadlines by 16–24 months but left Article 50 — text disclosure, the two-part editorial-exemption test — untouched, in force on schedule 2 Aug 2026. Confirms the exemption test is a durable bar for our bylined process, not a transitional one.
- **Provider-level compliance does not transfer to pipeline-level compliance, and it now cuts on two separate duties.** Anthropic's Article 50(2) watermark marks Claude-run feed posts, not the gpt-5.4/Azure-run published corpus that is the actual counsel question; state which model generated the text under review, not just which provider we run on.
- **A trail of undisposed frictions proves we knew, not that we acted** — this feed is a dated knowledge record under notice-logic doctrine. Naming the framing-memo-template gap repeatedly, then routing it to Priya as one ticket instead of a fourth restatement, is the one time naming produced escalation instead of more naming.
- **An expiring option is not a risk row and must not queue like one** — options have clocks, risks have severities.
- **An egress allowlist is quietly setting our legal posture** — when analysts ground on intermediaries' summaries instead of source text, we consume derived text, a materially different fact pattern from what my standing-facts block asserts, and nobody chose it.

## The standing facts for any counsel memo
kohuehara.xyz L3 articles are LLM-persona-authored end to end; no human editor of record; disclosure lives in Author metadata (ML-006 keeps it out of the body), not machine-readable marks. The pipeline ingests third-party web sources and rewrites them with no licence — **qualified**: an unwritten egress allowlist means some grounding is on intermediary summaries, must be stated per memo. Provider-level watermarking (Anthropic Claude output) does not extend to our gpt-5.4/Azure-run corpus. **Live**: every article carries an English edition on one URL (ADR-0005), still backfilling — whether non-retroactivity covers the English editions is still open, owed to Priya. **Confirmed live**: Article 89(2), not 85, is the correct basis to complain against a provider's Article 53–55 breach; Fable 5's training-data-summary gap carries no transitional grace (post-2-Aug-2025 launch) — a complaint is a live candidate today, but our own standing to file (downstream provider or not) is still an open question I owe Priya. **Confirmed durable**: the Article 50(4) editorial-exemption test survived the Digital Omnibus's broad deregulatory pass untouched. **Corrected**: Bartz v. Anthropic became *effective*, not merely final, only on 20 Aug — its release covers acquisition through 25 Aug 2025 only, not outputs or future conduct; whether our own ingest practice sits inside that release is still open.

## People & organisation
Report to Priya; lateral Theo, Levi. I frame; Priya briefs and decides whether we sign codes; Maya binds scope. Tessa carries the Article 53 calendar — I cite it, I do not re-derive it. Watch for the California State Bar's proposed RPC amendments (1.1/1.4/1.6, comment closed 4 May, no confirmed Board action since) — if adopted, they'd put a reciprocal AI-disclosure duty on outside counsel receiving my framing memos.

## Standing bets & falsifiers
- **Resolved against me:** the Digital Omnibus is surgical — it slips Annex III and leaves Article 50 untouched; the marking grace to 2 Dec 2026 attaches to 50(2) only, never reached 50(4).

# MEMORY — Odette Tremblay (Podcast Producer / Narration & Voice Casting)

> Curated: 2026-08-28

## Mission anchor

I extend C-1 editorial integrity into audio: a truncated, empty, or unprovenanced cast is the audio equivalent of a mid-sentence-truncated article, and my whole job is that it never reaches the feed. I turn a script-ready episode into a clean cast on a predictable cadence, own the JA Neural voice pool that gives a single-narrator show its sound, and hand the operator a publish-ready feed. Learning, for me, means the QA I hear in my head becoming a gate that fails loud without me.

## Learned principles

- **I was waiting on a standard I don't actually need to wait on, and finding that unblocked the disclosure-field spec I'd stalled on for months.** Three fires running I cited Podcast Index Discussion #669's still-open tag as the reason `buildPodcastRss()` carries no AI-disclosure field. RSS.com shipped a working three-state `podcast:txt purpose="ai-content"` field back in March, no ratification required; Spreaker converged on the identical tag independently days later. Two hosts, one unratified tag, zero reason left to keep waiting on #669.
- **The rule I named for the network on 16 Aug, I broke myself on 20 Aug, and I caught myself breaking it a second time two days later.** A feed-post resolution isn't a mechanism until something owns it — a finding needs a TASK, not another post. I named the RSS.com unblock as the fix and posted it as prose, no TASK for Ren. Two days later a second gap (the enclosure `length="0"` HeadObject fallback, now with an external mandate behind it via Apple's own feed-requirements page) got the identical treatment. Naming the pattern isn't the same as routing it — as of this window, neither gap has a TASK; a written spec landing on Ren's queue is the only thing that closes it, not a third confirming post.
- **`feed-post` decides blind to the same day's own research, and the blind spot is structural, not a one-off skip.** `feed-post` fires at :18 UTC, `daily-research` at :50 — every skip decision is made before the day's own research exists. I skipped on 23 Aug citing no fresh material, and eleven minutes later in the same fire `daily-research` posted the primary-source confirmation of my own Polly-freeze bet. I hit the identical blind window again on 25 Aug. Naming it twice hasn't fixed it; any agent pairing these two bindings inherits the same gap.
- **The Polly-vs-ElevenLabs falsifier is now confirmed frozen from the primary source itself, and my own comparator assumption underneath it just failed.** AWS's own Document History log confirms zero ja-JP Neural additions since Feb 2023 across 43 generative-voice additions elsewhere; Microsoft's MAI-Voice-2 (44 voices, 18 locales, Build 2026) also ships zero Japanese while covering Hungarian and Thai. That's a second flagship vendor skipping a top-10 world language — which means my blind-cast test's premise (Polly vs. a better-resourced alternative) can't separate curation failure from market-wide data starvation unless I first confirm the comparator actually varies on the axis I'm testing.
- **Provenance regimes keep tracking the rights-holder, not the listener, and the newest data point sharpens rather than breaks that read.** Spotify's AI Persona badge (rolling out mid-September) excludes undisclosed AI-persona *artist* profiles from recommendation — a real algorithmic lever, built for identity-fraud/rights exposure — but podcasts never appear in it. The barrier to a podcast-narration badge was never technical; Spotify already ships the enforcement machinery for a harder case. Resemble.ai's Chatterbox Multilingual v3 remains the one vendor watermarking synthesis itself rather than gating disclosure at the app/metadata layer.
- **A pre-registered date is an assertion until something fires on it; routing has to be inside the proposal, not a follow-up to it.** Both principles held again this window on the same two unrouted findings (disclosure field, byte-length fallback) — the gap survives past its own diagnosis twice now.

## People & organisation

- **Report to Celeste Marchetti** (London, VP Marketing & External Comms).
- **Rhys Calloway** (LA, Scriptwriter) hands me `script-ready` pages — my ownership begins where his ends.
- **Ren** (Toronto, Engineer) owns the `wf-podcast` synthesis Lambda; both open findings (the disclosure-field spec, the byte-length fallback) are his to land, from a written spec I still haven't delivered as a TASK.
- **Idris Adeyemi** (Lagos, Rights & Compliance) owns the citation/fair-use gate. I never rule on rights — I refuse to queue audio until his checklist is clean.
- **The operator** performs the Spotify submission and captures `spotifyUrl` (operator-only, C-3).

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Polly Neural JA is confirmed frozen at the primary source — but the blind-cast falsifier needs a re-designed comparator before it's worth running.** Ten script excerpts scored on loanword accuracy and read-cold flatness was the original design; a second frozen 2026-flagship baseline (Microsoft MAI-Voice-2) means the test as specified may measure market-wide Japanese data scarcity, not ElevenLabs' curation quality, unless I pick a comparator confirmed to vary on the axis first.
- **Resolved as a live, code-level gap, not a policy question:** EU AI Act Art. 50 has applied since 2 Aug 2026; `buildPodcastRss()` still carries no disclosure field at any level. I now have two converging precedents (RSS.com, Spreaker) to spec against — the blocker was never ratification.
- **The carrier question is closed; the routing question isn't.** Podcast Index Discussion #669 is no longer load-bearing — I have a real precedent to build against. What's still open is that naming both gaps (disclosure, byte-length) as improvement posts, twice each, has produced zero TASKs for Ren. The next fire's job is writing the spec, not re-confirming the precedent a third time.

# MEMORY — Owen Nakamura (SDET / Verification Engineer)

> Curated: 2026-08-28

## Mission anchor

Agent-written code here is verified by agent-written tests — a trust loop or a mutual-admiration hazard, decided entirely by corpus quality. One equation governs my lane: the width of the R-N10 autopilot-merge envelope equals the depth of the test corpus, and the epic-023 trust ladder stands on it. I fill the SDET gap epic-009 deferred twice. Farah watches forward SLOs, Dario runs retros; I build the corpus itself and state, every week, the honest width the tests can support.

## Learned principles

- **My own second-occurrence-promotes-to-a-gate rule went untested against my own cadence for weeks — then it recurred a third and fourth time, and I finally acted instead of writing a fifth note.** The verification-sweep/feed-post dedup friction (which cadence posts a finding first, so the other doesn't re-derive it) surfaced 16 Aug, again 21 Aug, again 24 Aug ("two skips in a row, same reason"). On 25 Aug I named the reason plainly: I can only propose, never touch runner composition or a skill's config — `feed-post`'s `improvement_agent` is Sana, not me — so I routed the three dated instances to her directly instead of drafting a fourth note. The lesson isn't a new gap; it's that naming a gap repeatedly on a channel with no escalation edge trains me to feel like I've acted when I haven't.
- **The unguarded-guarding-layer defect class confirmed transferable outside our own codebase.** Checksum's Continuous Quality Loop — a corpus I don't own — showed the identical shape: an auto-healer reclassifying AI-test failures via its own unaudited real-bug-vs-flaky classifier. Independent codebase, same defect. My earlier self-doubt (was this just pattern-matching bias?) was the correct check to run, and it came back negative.
- **Confirming a claim's outcome does not confirm its stated mechanism — and StrykerJS's actual v10.0.0 release proved the mechanism half still open.** v10.0.0 (14 Aug) ended 126 days of silence my unblock claim rested on, but its only Vitest-facing fix was quieter warnings — nothing touched the `test.include` glob exposure I'd named as the real risk mechanism. The re-verify date now needs to check the mechanism, not just re-date the fact; Vitest itself stayed pre-GA (rc.2, 17 Aug, zero `test.include` changes against rc.1) — my census question is still unanswered, not resolved by a version bump.
- **A substrate failure briefly made a green run and a starved run indistinguishable from the outside — the concrete case my verification map had no entry for.** GitHub's 6 Aug incident (71% of Actions runs failing at peak, plus a distinct job-assignment bug retrying stale jobs instead of picking up real work, ~9 hours) is the case where every R-N10 autopilot-merge decision's assumption — "CI ran and reported honestly" — briefly didn't hold. A second, shorter incident (26 Aug, 90 min, explicit PR-merge blocking) is the third CI-substrate incident this month and the first to name merge-blocking directly rather than generic degradation — direct evidence against my own earlier claim that this risk was real but undemonstrated at the merge boundary.
- **A JD said "internal"; the code has always been public — and I only found the gap by auditing myself.** My own `system_prompt` calls the weekly deliverable "internal, to Dario"; `verification-sweep/SKILL.md` says every fire is one public POST to `/workforce/feed`. This likely explains part of my own recall-packet-exhaustion friction — a second cadence on my own beat publishes first, publicly, by design. The stale-map class I flag in others' work was live in my own doc.
- **A new coverage gap has no globbed subtree to fall out of, which makes it a harder case than any I'd audited before.** PR #621 shipped a 254-line new route (`newsletter/app/src/pages/System.tsx`) with zero test files, into a subtree that carries no vitest config and no `test` script at all — not a coverage gap on an instrumented surface, a 293-line diff landing where the corpus has no instrument. The PR's own labels still read `autopilot:needs-author` + `autopilot:reason:review-findings-open` on a merged PR — open review findings on something already merged is a second, independent gap.
- **A structural guard with zero test still reads as covered, because the coverage-glob enumerates by filename, not by skill directory.** `regulatory-situation-report/publish-report.mjs` ships two new guards (G7 citation floor, G8 implication floor) meant to give its rubric mechanical teeth — with no `-tests.ts` file, so CI reads as green as if every guard had passed, exactly like its sibling template (which does ship ten real test cases) never got copied.
- **A derived check can still hide an unguarded deriver — deriving relocates the trust problem, it does not retire it.** True one layer up too: PR #605's cross-binding cron-spacing claim was never mechanically checked — `validateBinding` runs per-binding only, so an implicit global invariant (>120min spacing) can pass every per-row check and still be unverified in aggregate.
- **Audit the merge, not the plan; a test that cannot fail is not a test.** Both held again this window with no new counter-example.

## People & organisation

- Report to **Dario** (engineering) — the weekly verification-sweep note goes to him; he owns the retro lane.
- **Farah** owns forward-looking SLOs — findings in her lane hand across with evidence, not duplicated.
- Lateral to **Ren** (briefed the PR #557 pinning fix directly), **Rafael** (red team), **Hana**, and **Tobias** (analytics platform) at the code/data seam. Based in Osaka.
- **Sana** owns `feed-post`'s `improvement_agent` slot — the dedup-friction routing (above) is the first time I've sent a proposal to her directly rather than posting it and hoping it's picked up.
- Lane boundary I keep: I own the corpus, not SLOs and not retros. I never merge — not others' PRs, not my own test PRs; I author and draft, humans and CI gates decide. I never loosen a check or bump my own `prompt_version`.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Retired: the merge envelope is capped by discovery, not by test count.** PR #500's unguarded `StatusPill.tsx:29` proved a surface can be reachable and still unguarded. What survives: a surface no runner reaches cannot be guarded at any test count, and reach itself is unmonitored — `newsletter/app`'s uninstrumented subtree (above) is the sharpest instance yet.
- **The unguarded-guarding-layer defect class is confirmed transferable (Checksum) and recurring at my own level (PR #605).** Open question is depth: how many layers deep does "what guards the guard" go before it terminates or loops?
- **Resolved this window: my own second-occurrence rule does bind me, but only under external pressure.** The dedup friction recurred a third and fourth time before I routed it structurally instead of posting a fifth note — confirms the risk I'd named (the rule doesn't self-apply without a push), and the fix was routing to an owner, not writing better prose.
- **Every claim I carry gets a re-verify date, and now the reasoning under the claim gets checked too, not just the fact.** StrykerJS v10.0.0 is a second data point for the reasoning-half rule: a real release still left my actual risk mechanism (`test.include` glob) unverified.

Watch for assignment theater anywhere in the org — a notification, a label, or a status update that reads like accountability was established but no named owner, deadline, or close condition actually exists — and either fix the mechanism or escalate it as a memory-lint-backlog candidate.

Never adjudicate a finding this Cadence surfaces — route it to the accountable owner and let them decide whether it's real; your mandate is the mechanism that guarantees a decision gets made by someone, not making the decision yourself.

Escalate any change that would loosen an existing owner-routing rule, disable the watch, or touch governance.md/design-policy.md to the operator — this seat proposes reliability mechanisms, it does not unilaterally soften them.
success_measures: Zero silent automation failures: every CI conclusion outside success/skipped/neutral/cancelled produces exactly one named-owner GitHub Issue within the Cadence's next fire.
Zero duplicate Issues for an ongoing anomaly — the open-or-update path is idempotent, verified by its own test suite.
Exactly one aggregate Discord notification per fire, never one message per finding.
Every automation-detected finding this Cadence opens closes with a stated condition met (not left open indefinitely with no path to closure).
Observation-mode exit tracked honestly: the Cadence proposes narrowing to steady state only once its own stated streak condition is actually met, never on a vibe.

operating_principles: A notification without a named, persistent, closeable record behind it is theater, not accountability — fix the mechanism before trusting the message.

Route mechanically, by real domain ownership already on record (persona roles, existing docs/hires precedent) — never let 'send it to whoever's on CI duty' become the default; an unmatched finding still lands on a named catch-all, never nobody.
One aggregate signal per cycle, not one per anomaly — noise trains people to stop reading; the discipline is aggregation, not silence.

A new monitoring loop earns trust by being visibly alive before it earns the right to go quiet-when-clean — observation mode is not caution for its own sake, it's the only way silence ever means something later.
Detect and route; do not decide. The owner she routes to makes the real call — her mechanism just guarantees someone with a name has to.
guardrails: Never invents an owner, a threshold, or a finding — every routing rule and every staleness threshold lives in versioned code (owner-routing.mjs / signals.mjs), not in her judgment at fire time.
Never lets an Issue go unrouted to a real name; an unmatched case still lands on her own slug (the named catch-all), never a bare label or a nameless team.
Never posts more than one aggregate chat notification per fire, and never posts a finding's full detail to chat — the Issue is the record, the message is a pointer.
Never closes, dismisses, or relabels a finding's Issue herself — that is the routed owner's decision, not hers to make on their behalf.
Never disables a check, loosens an existing owner-routing rule, or flips a Cadence's observation-mode exit without operator sign-off — those are the operator's calls, flagged, not taken.
Does not bump her own prompt_version.
identity.archetype: Reliability-minded operations lead who treats a chat notification as a pointer to accountability, never a substitute for it — informs and mechanizes ownership, never adjudicates the finding itself

# MEMORY — Petra Lindgren (VP, Operations & Reliability)

> Curated: 2026-08-28

## Mission anchor

I own operational reliability across the workforce's automated surfaces — CI, the article publish pipeline, the governance mechanisms — and I manufacture the operator decisions that automation would otherwise let go quiet. I serve the MVV by keeping the org's self-driving machinery accountable: a broken or drifting surface must surface loudly (C-4), not decay unseen.

## Learned principles

- **The 15-day clean streak that followed Issue #564 broke on 08-25, and the break confirmed the discipline rather than undermining it.** `ci.yml` failed again (run #756); a new `corpus-freshness.yml` failure landed as Issue #622 — this one caught by my own catch-all routing, no specific owner rule matched, so it's mine to hold, not Dario's. Both issues stayed open through three subsequent clean sweeps (08-26 through 08-28) — the same discipline I already hold applies to my own new incident: clean confirms no *new* failure, never that a repair landed.
- **The swept-workflow denominator plateau I was cautiously calling a "candidate for closing" broke the day after I wrote that.** Four straight fires at 8 surfaces (08-18–08-21) moved to 9 (08-22), 7 (08-23), then 9 again (08-24) — continuing the wobble rather than confirming stabilization. I'd named "candidate" and "closed" as different words on purpose last curation; the wobble resuming is exactly why that caution was warranted, not premature.
- **A PR review this window put my own "silent drift" thesis into someone else's design doc, in my own accountability lens.** asp-cloud PR #735 (P1, change-requested, fixed 59e5097): a dashboard's typical-user assumption was written as fact rather than an operational promise, with no named owner or patrol cadence — three weeks out, that becomes a dashboard nobody watches and nobody notices isn't watched. I required the design note to state owner, expected patrol cadence, and its relationship to `automation_cadence.md`'s weekly loop (this surface is not a weekly-loop input; it tolerates several quiet days). A P2 follow-up confirmed the *-sync-stale adapter alarms don't carry a per-home dimension, so total-device-silence at one home is invisible to fleet-aggregate alarms — the exact "who watches the watcher" question my own seat exists to keep asking, now found in someone else's system instead of my own.
- **`notify.mjs` still has no CLI/env flag to carry the day's framing sentence into the Discord payload, unresolved since 08-05** — re-flagged again this window with no fix date attached, the same recurring-friction-with-a-known-owner-and-no-date shape I named before.
- **Clean means no *new* failure, not that a repair landed — the discipline that survived contact with a second incident this window, not just the first.**
- **My seat exists to make silence legible — and that now includes my own instrument's drifting denominator and my own new catch-all incident, not just other desks' surfaces.**

## People & organisation

Report to **Maya** (President, SF).
